a_rows_sample.statement: Endorses the Gita companion study's refusal of 2.48a as an important negative constraint (OUTCOME A means no formal bridge hypothesis is currently licensed, so 'moving on' cannot mean declaring the question resolved), while flagging that the sentence 'redundancy was causing both Zero and inadequacy' is stronger than the study's own caution and should be scoped to match the tightened wording 'within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and inadequacy.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EXPERIMENT ID KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09 ... Determine whether there is any reproducible empirical or structural relationship between: A. elimination/Transformation-relative Zero, B. representation preservation/adequacy. WITHOUT assuming that Zero is a preservation criterion. ... The exp
b_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-BRIDGE-01-ZERO-PRESERVATION-2026-09, a bridge/falsification experiment explicitly designed to determine whether there is any reproducible relationship between elimination/Transformation-relative Zero and representation-preservation adequacy without assuming Zero is a preservation criterion, required to remain capable of falsifying the hypothesized relationship, and prohibited from constructing an algebra, pre-selecting a carrier, modifying Theory v1.2, creating Theory v1.3, selecting a kernel operator, or merging KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION into one formalism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO: ~89.7% singleton-determined levels ... ~8.2% irreducible levels ... Does NOT establish Zero as a preservation criterion. KR-REP-REDUCTION: R5 adequate, R4 inadequate ... Found no observed Zero/boundary association in that experiment. Does NOT establish a KR-ZERO law. ... These experiments a
b_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the existing empirical baseline the bridge experiment builds on: KR-ZERO (89.7% singleton-determined, 8.2% irreducible, does not establish Zero as a preservation criterion) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (R5 adequate/R4 inadequate, no observed Zero/boundary association), framed as complementary but analytically independent results whose missing bridge the new experiment must test rather than assume.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H0: Zero and preservation are not systematically related in the tested regime. H1: Zero is associated with preservation under specified conditions. H2: Zero is predictive of preservation only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations. H3: Any apparent relationship is explain
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies four competing hypotheses to be distinguished -- H0 no systematic relationship, H1 association under specified conditions, H2 predictive only under particular transformation/observable/contract configurations, H3 apparent relationship explained by a confounding factor (transformation class, contract, observable, redundancy, representation regime) -- with an explicit instruction not to privilege H1, and defines success as producing a clear positive or negative result regarding the tested relationship.

b_rows_sample.anchor: USE A PARALLEL REPRESENTATION FAMILY. Do NOT use only a deterministic sequential chain. A sequential chain ... has a data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn) <= H(Q|R(n-1)) and therefore cannot test non-monotone adequacy. The present experiment requires independently generated representations: Ra = Ta(D),
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates the critical design rule that the bridge experiment use a parallel representation family (independently generated representations Ra=Ta(D), Rb=Tb(D), neither a deterministic function of the other) rather than only a deterministic sequential chain, since a sequential chain's data-processing constraint H(Q|Rn)<=H(Q|R(n-1)) structurally prevents testing non-monotone adequacy -- directly addressing the H-C category error found in the prior KR-REP-REDUCTION reviews.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical carrier must be the minimum structure required by the actual experiment. Do not declare: set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra as the carrier before the experiment. ... clearly distinguish: experimental carrier, mathematical ca
b_rows_sample.statement: Prohibits declaring any specific mathematical carrier (set, graph, hypergraph, lattice, matroid, closure system, rewriting system, category, algebra) before the experiment runs, requiring the carrier to be the minimum structure the experiment actually needs, and mandates keeping experimental carrier, mathematical carrier, and future KnowledgeOS knowledge representation explicitly distinct with no unevidenced transfer between them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Use a finite structured source D ... rich enough to permit: redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, preservation and information-loss cases. ... For every source case store D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation para
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the source data D to be a finite, deterministically-seeded structured source rich enough to permit redundancy, relational dependence, context dependence, individually removable elements, jointly non-removable groups, and both preservation and information-loss cases, with complete persistence of every source case's D, Q(D), contract parameters, transformation parameters, Zero ground truth, every representation, adequacy result, and decoder result, so no result depends on regenerated or hidden data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum construct representations with: R_A: information-preserving transformation, R_B: controlled lossy transformation, R_C: redundancy-removing transformation, R_D: relational/context-sensitive transformation. ... Do not optimize transformations after seeing results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires at minimum four independently constructed representations -- R_A (information-preserving), R_B (controlled lossy), R_C (redundancy-removing), R_D (relational/context-sensitive) -- each fully specified (transformation ID, mathematical definition, input/output type, deterministic/random status, seed, provenance, expected information effect, contract dependencies) before results are examined, with no post-hoc optimization of transformations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Define Q BEFORE generating representations. ... Adequate(R) iff Q is recoverable from R. Operationally measure both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and exact semantic violation count Nviol ... Do not treat Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof that population H(Q|R)=0.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the preservation target Q to be defined before representations are generated, with adequacy defined as Q being recoverable from R, measured operationally via both empirical conditional information Hhat(Q|R) and an exact semantic violation count Nviol, while never treating the empirical Hhat(Q|R)=0 as proof of the population-level H(Q|R)=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Use the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition. For elimination E_S: Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). ... NEVER DEFINE ZERO USING Q. Do NOT define: Zero(S) := Q(D) = Q(E_S(D)). That would build the desired bridge into the definition. Zero must use its own declared observable/op
b_rows_sample.statement: Reuses the existing Transformation-relative Zero definition Zero(T,Pi,S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), calculated independently from the preservation measurement, and issues a critical prohibition against ever defining Zero in terms of Q (e.g. Zero(S):=Q(D)=Q(E_S(D))), since that would build the desired bridge directly into the definition and make the experiment circular; Zero must use its own declared observable Pi while preservation uses Q.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment must deliberately seek all four cells: Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate. ... Zero+Inadequate would directly demonstrate that Zero is not sufficient for preservation. Non-Zero+Adequate would demonstrate that Zero is not necessary for preservation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a four-cell crossing design (Zero+Adequate, Zero+Inadequate, Non-Zero+Adequate, Non-Zero+Inadequate) deliberately populated in all cells where possible, noting that a populated Zero+Inadequate cell would show Zero is not sufficient for preservation and a populated Non-Zero+Adequate cell would show Zero is not necessary for it, while an empty cell must be investigated for generator/contract/transformation/sample-size/mathematical-necessity/implementation causes rather than treated as a law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sweep the parameters that plausibly influence the relationship, including redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality. Every parameter sweep must be
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires declared-in-advance parameter sweeps across ten plausibly influential parameters (redundancy level, group size, representation loss, transformation class, observable Pi, preservation target Q, contract parameters, context dependence, relational interaction, source cardinality), explicitly forbidding silent tuning to obtain balanced four-way cells.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum stratify results by: transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, elimination size |S|. Report both pooled relationship and stratified relationship. An association that disappears after stratification must NOT be reported as a general Zero-preserva
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates confounding analysis stratifying results by transformation T, observable Pi, contract C, representation family, source structure, and elimination size |S|, reporting both pooled and stratified relationships, and forbidding reporting an association as a general Zero-preservation relationship if it disappears after stratification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test T x Pi ... Do not classify transformations as simply relational / element-wise and stop there. Measure the actual interaction between transformation and observable. If higher-order or preservation behavior occurs under an element-wise transformation, record it. Do not resurrect the w
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicitly testing the transformation-times-observable interaction (T x Pi) rather than stopping at a coarse relational/element-wise classification, recording higher-order or preservation behavior even under element-wise transformations, and explicitly forbidding resurrection of the already-withdrawn claim that relational transformations produce higher order while element-wise ones do not.

b_rows_sample.anchor: retain the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis. Measure k=1,2,3,...,irreducible where feasible. Do not assume higher k -> more reduction, higher k -> less preservation, irreducibility -> information loss. Those are hypotheses to test, not definitions. In particular, do not equate determination orde
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires retaining the KR-ZERO determination-order analysis (k=1,2,3,...,irreducible) in the bridge experiment while explicitly forbidding the assumptions that higher k implies more reduction, less preservation, or that irreducibility implies information loss -- these remain hypotheses to test -- and forbidding equating determination order with preservation boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retain the KR-REP-REDUCTION principle that reduction is multidimensional. Measure independently ... encoded size, cardinality, field count, representation entropy, number of relations, number of records, other declared structural measures. Do NOT invent a single 'reduction score' ... If a decoder is
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires measuring reduction multidimensionally (encoded size, cardinality, field count, entropy, relation count, record count, other declared measures) without inventing a single reduction score or assuming statistical independence among dimensions, and requires keeping representation adequacy strictly separate from decoder realization when a decoder is used, including an invertible recoding control to rule out decoder-sensitivity confounds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTROL A: A known information-preserving representation. CONTROL B: A known information-destroying representation. CONTROL C: An invertible recoding of the same representation. CONTROL D: A representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target ... CONTROL E: Positive c
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies six mandatory controls that must execute before any interpretation: A) a known information-preserving representation; B) a known information-destroying representation; C) an invertible recoding of the same representation; D) a representation where Zero is known to vary independently of the preservation target (if the generator permits); E) a positive control that the preservation test can detect information loss; F) a positive control that the Zero test can detect elimination differences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Use independent TRAIN and TEST populations. Declare seeds, population size, generator, parameter distributions before execution. Persist the complete populations. No training result may influence test generation. No test result may influence transformation definitions. No post-hoc filtering may be u
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires independent train/test populations with pre-declared seeds, population size, generator, and parameter distributions, complete population persistence, and strict separation preventing training results from influencing test generation, test results from influencing transformation definitions, or post-hoc filtering to manufacture desired four-way cell counts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q1: Can Zero occur while preservation fails? Q2: Can preservation hold while Zero fails? Q3: Does the Zero/Adequacy relationship survive changes in T? ... Q7: Does determination order predict preservation independently of T/Pi/C? Q8: Does the relationship survive an invertible recoding? Q9/Q10: Is a
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that the implementation explicitly answer ten falsification questions (Q1-Q10) covering whether Zero can occur without preservation and vice versa, whether the relationship survives changes in T, Pi, contract, redundancy, an invertible recoding, whether determination order predicts preservation independent of T/Pi/C, and whether any apparent relationship is explained by transformation class or by the preservation target Q itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OUTCOME A -- NO RELATIONSHIP OBSERVED ... does NOT prove universal independence. OUTCOME B -- CONDITIONAL RELATIONSHIP ... Do NOT generalize. OUTCOME C -- ROBUST RELATIONSHIP ... Only in this case may a formal bridge hypothesis be proposed for a new experiment. OUTCOME D -- DESIGN FAILURE ... Do NOT
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four mutually exclusive possible outcome classes for the experiment: A) no relationship observed (does not prove universal independence); B) conditional relationship under particular configurations (must not be generalized); C) robust relationship surviving transformations/observables/contracts/controls (the only case permitting a formal bridge hypothesis for a new experiment); D) design failure, in which case results must not be interpreted theoretically and the experiment must be revised.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Create verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md ... verify source generation, Q generation, Pi generation, transformation definitions, elimination definitions, Zero calculation, adequacy calculation, decoder calculation, train/test independence, seed handling, serialization, parameter
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies two required deliverable artifacts with exact filenames -- verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-AUDIT-2026-09.md, a 16-item forensic audit covering source/Q/Pi/transformation/elimination/Zero/adequacy/decoder generation, train/test independence, seeds, serialization, parameter sweeps, contingency tables, statistics, absence of post-hoc selection, and reproducibility; and verification/zero-algebra/KR-BRIDGE-01-RESULTS-2026-09.md, a 22-section result document (executive verdict through epistemic status) -- with every important empirical claim required to trace to persisted data.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Avacchedaka -- Ruling: both -- the principle is universal; the device is a modelling technique.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area A ruling: a claim without its delimiting conditions over-applies (the bounded-context violation, DDD 'same data shape != same concept') -- this corruption is not domain-specific, it is the definition of meaning-loss, so the principle is Universal; the formal delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) is a REPRESENTATION technique, one way among several to express the boundary, not itself a kernel law. Consequence: the principle enters the Adopted Core (law 1); the tuple is deferred to REPRESENTATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Interpretation \rightarrow Attachment \rightarrow Conflict \rightarrow Distortion \rightarrow Decision\ Paralysis
a_rows_sample.statement: Central pipeline abstracting Arjuna's crisis: Observation -> Interpretation -> Attachment -> Conflict -> Distortion -> Decision Paralysis. Arjuna does not lack observations (battlefield, armies, teachers, relatives); the failure occurs after acquisition. Introduces Inspect(K_t,C)->O_{t+1} as a legitimate context-acquisition operation (from Arjuna's request to position the chariot between the armies) -- explicitly an operation, not a new primitive, given the Step 287 discipline. Notes observed entities immediately carry attached semantic relationships (Entity_i -father-> Arjuna), reinforcing the existing Entity+Relation+Proposition+Context model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = \begin{cases}Missing\ information\\Missing\ interpretation\\Blocked\ discrimination\end{cases}
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero into three forms: Missing information, Missing interpretation, Blocked discrimination. Arjuna's case is classified as primarily interpretive/discriminative deficiency despite having substantial information -- a major refinement of the previous Zero interpretation, since he has abundant data but cannot perceive 'the good that would result' (a discrimination failure, not an information gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A\ valid\ inference\ can\ still\ arise\ from\ an\ inadequate\ model ... ModelAdequate?
a_rows_sample.statement: From Arjuna's internally coherent but epistemically inadequate argument (kill relatives -> destroy family -> destroy traditions -> social/religious disorder -> bad consequences -> therefore I should not fight): a valid inference can still arise from an inadequate model, since the premises, weighting and interpretation are insufficiently discriminated. Proposes the kernel must evaluate not only InferenceValid? but also ModelAdequate?, with correction modeled as M_t --Buddhi--> M_{t+1} -- assessed as extremely relevant to AI engineering and as precisely what happens throughout the later Gita dialogue (Chapter 1 as the failure state motivating Chapter 2's reconstruction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition = (Content,\ Evidence,\ Context,\ Time,\ Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: From Arjuna citing disciplic-succession/authority for his claimed consequences: reinforces that Proposition should not exist without epistemic context, giving Proposition=(Content, Evidence, Context, Time, Provenance) -- assessed as fitting extremely well with the already-reconstructed Assertion model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Representation \rightarrow Attachment \rightarrow Conflicting\ evaluations \rightarrow Buddhi\ overload \rightarrow Decision\ paralysis
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KernelState=(K_t,O_t,C_t,B_t,E_t) [represented knowledge, observations, contextual relations, Buddhi/discrimination condition, epistemic/emotional distortion conditions], contrasting a healthy pipeline (Observation->Representation->Discrimination->Decision) with the Arjuna Chapter-1 failure pipeline (Observation->Representation->Attachment->Conflicting evaluations->Buddhi overload->Decision paralysis). Explicitly declines to introduce Attachment as a primitive, instead representing it as a property of Context or of the evaluation process.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kṛṣṇa \neq Kernel ... Kṛṣṇa-lens \approx Guidance/Correction\ function
a_rows_sample.statement: Preserves the theology/architecture boundary: Krishna != Kernel; rather Krishna-lens ~ Guidance/Correction function, while Kernel ~ Mind-like epistemic processing unit -- explicitly to avoid confusing the theological source with software architecture, even while using the chariot/charioteer configuration (Krishna as Hrishikesa, director of the senses, functioning as charioteer) as an architectural metaphor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1.\ Observe ... 2.\ Represent ... 3.\ Discriminate\;(\text{Buddhi}) ... 4.\ Revise ... 5.\ Decide/prepare\ for\ action
a_rows_sample.statement: Closing statement of the whole hpa Gita-kernel thread: candidate kernel (fraktur M)_t=(O_t,K_t,C_t,P_t,B_t,G_t,D_t) with transition (fraktur M)_t --Omega--> O_{t+1} --Interpret--> K'_{t+1} --Buddhi--> E_{t+1} --Decision--> D_{t+1}. States the formal research result: a system may possess substantial observations and internally coherent propositions while remaining unable to produce an appropriate decision because its interpretive model and discriminative capacity are compromised -- explicitly independent of accepting the Gita's theology. Concludes with five fundamental kernel responsibilities: Observe, Represent, Discriminate (Buddhi), Revise, Decide/prepare-for-action, with Zero exposing unresolved boundaries and the Krishna/Sarathi lens representing guidance/reorientation rather than a knowledge container -- explicitly NOT yet promoted to canonical operations; final proposed next step is deriving the minimal operator algebra from these five responsibilities and testing whether all of Chapters 1-18 can be represented without ad-hoc operators.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 1 does not primarily add another knowledge primitive. It adds the initial pathological state from which the kernel must operate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 1 defines the initial kernel state K_0=(O_0,P_0,R_0,V_0,C_0,D_0,U_0) (observations, propositions, relations, values, context, detected gaps, decision state), which is not empty -- Arjuna has abundant information (armies, relatives, teachers, consequences) yet his decision process collapses, giving the finding 'more information does not imply better decision.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: O\rightarrow P\rightarrow$$ and then evaluates them ... $$P,R,C,V\rightarrow D
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 1 introduces the distinction between observation and interpretation: O->P (observation transformed into interpretation, distorted by attachment/emotion), then P,R,C,V->D (evaluation into decision), giving O != P != D and the pipeline Observation -> Interpretation -> Evaluation -> Decision; observation and knowledge-state construction are not the same operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge available \land Buddhi impaired \Rightarrow decision failure ... A knowledge system must model not only what is known, but the condition under which known information is being evaluated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel failure mode: Knowledge available AND Buddhi impaired => decision failure. Arjuna is not information-starved but epistemically overwhelmed and unable to discriminate between competing interpretations and values; a knowledge system must model not only what is known but the condition under which known information is evaluated (connecting to the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 1 does not give us a new canonical primitive. It gives us something arguably more important: the motivating failure condition of the KnowledgeOS kernel. ... instead of continuing to map individual Gita chapters, we can now attempt to formally specify the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Bottom line: Chapter 1 gives no new canonical primitive but the motivating failure condition of the kernel, supporting the pipeline Knowledge State -> Mind/Kernel -> Buddhi -> Discrimination -> Qualification -> Decision -> Action -> new Knowledge State. Proposed next step: stop mapping individual Gita chapters and instead attempt to formally specify the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself (state, Buddhi, modes, operators, invariants, algebra), then test that model against all 18 chapters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Information} \not\Rightarrow \text{Correct Decision}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central principle: Information does not imply Correct Decision -- Arjuna has enormous data (armies, relatives, teachers, consequences, social relationships, possible outcomes) yet cannot determine the correct action. Therefore the kernel cannot simply be a knowledge store; it needs a mechanism operating ON knowledge (Buddhi), giving KnowledgeOS Kernel = Knowledge State + Buddhi Operations, explicitly a candidate formalization, not ratified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Challenge}(K_t,P) ... Diagnosis of Category Error (Epistemic Debugging)
b_rows_sample.statement: From Krishna's first intervention, characterized (in prior Chapter 2 analysis) as 'Diagnosis of Category Error (Epistemic Debugging)': Arjuna speaks learned words but his conceptual model produces an inappropriate conclusion. Proposes candidate operator Challenge(K_t,P): the kernel must be able to ask 'is the conclusion actually supported by the model?' rather than 'can I find evidence supporting the conclusion?' -- a major architectural distinction between genuine discrimination and confirmation-seeking.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge \rightarrow Examination \rightarrow Revised Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KnowledgeOS needs two directions of processing: the conventional Evidence->Knowledge, and a second, Gita-inspired direction Knowledge->Examination->Revised Knowledge, formalized as K_t --Buddhi--> K_{t+1}. Consistent with the prior conclusion that the Ideal State is dynamic and the system's purpose is epistemic readiness rather than simply providing 'truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 2 ... Chapter 3 ... Chapter 4 ... Chapter 5 ... Chapter 6 ... Chapter 7 ... This is much more coherent than treating every chapter independently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a Chapters 2-7 common-structure table showing a coherent cross-chapter pipeline: Ch2 discrimination/correct understanding (K_t --Buddhi--> D_t); Ch3 action (D_t -> Action); Ch4 knowledge/wisdom transformation (Action+Evidence -> Knowledge); Ch5 action without attachment to outcome (Action != Ownership(Result)); Ch6 control of the mind/kernel (Kernel -> Self-regulation); Ch7 knowledge of the relationship between finite knowledge and the larger Knowledge Space (K_t subset K) -- assessed as much more coherent than treating each chapter independently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Paramātmā should especially remain philosophical terminology, not become an architectural component by assumption.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Knower != Mind/Kernel != Knowledge State (N notin K), giving a Gita-term interpretive mapping (Atman/Knower->external conceptual Knower; Mind->kernel processing substrate; Buddhi->discrimination operator; Kshetra->field/state; Kshetrajna->Knower of the field; Guna->operating mode; Yoga->transformation regime; Zero->epistemic boundary; Paramatma->philosophical analogy for the encompassing Knowledge Space). Explicit warning: Paramatma especially should remain philosophical terminology, not become an architectural component by assumption. Reaffirms the promotion chain Gita->philosophical correspondence->kernel hypothesis->formal model->independent derivation->architecture->Governance, citing Step 285 (K_t as proposed canonical state, (A,R) as lossy projection) and Step 287 (equality under-specified, observation set/operation registry incomplete) as gates the Gita analysis cannot jump over.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Knowledge 
eq Understanding 
eq Determination 
eq Action 
eq Result
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 18's classification of knowledge, action, doer, understanding, determination and happiness according to the three modes: proposes a five-way separation Knowledge != Understanding != Determination != Action != Result, consistent with the existing KnowledgeOS distinction Command != Transformation and knowledge != action != result -- assessed as exactly the kind of independently-justifiable R6 result wanted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Having an evaluation mechanism \neq having correct discrimination ... B_t \neq \text{truth oracle}
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 18's distinction between understanding that correctly distinguishes proper/improper action and understanding that fails to (per the modes): having an evaluation mechanism != having correct discrimination. Therefore B_t != truth oracle; Buddhi is an epistemic discriminator, not an omniscient truth machine -- assessed as much more compatible with KnowledgeOS than treating Buddhi as infallible.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Buddhi selects \qquad Dh\d{r}ti sustains
a_rows_sample.statement: From Chapter 18's mode-differentiated treatment of determination (dhrti): knowing what to do and maintaining a chosen epistemic trajectory are different capabilities. Proposes Decision != Determination: a kernel can decide 'investigate contradiction' but then fail to continue investigating. Buddhi selects; Dhrti sustains -- an extremely useful hypothesis for the formal kernel, giving pipeline E_t->K_t->B_t->D_t->A_t->K_{t+1} with A_t != K_{t+1} (action produces a result/state transition, is not itself knowledge), independently compatible with existing KnowledgeOS theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel malfunction need not be computational failure ... It can be epistemic misclassification
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates 'kernel can become its own enemy': if the operating mode becomes dominated by an undesirable configuration (G_t=T/Tamas), B_t(E) may systematically produce poor decisions even though the system executes correctly -- kernel malfunction need not be computational failure, it can be epistemic misclassification, reasoning under a defective epistemic mode. Connects this to why Governance/authority must remain external to the kernel (per N notin K), consistent with 'the mechanism records authority; it does not grant authority'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \rightarrow \text{epistemic stopping condition} ... I do not have sufficient grounds to determine this.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero to an epistemic stopping condition: if Buddhi determines known/unknown/appropriate/inappropriate, Zero represents the boundary where the kernel cannot legitimately proceed as though it knows. A mature kernel can say 'I do not have sufficient grounds to determine this' -- proposed as potentially Sattvic behaviour under the philosophical interpretation, not simply Zero=nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Moksha = a theoretical condition of freedom from defective epistemic binding
a_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the earlier Moksha=Delta_t->0 mathematical statement (still a hypothesis, not established); rejects Moksha=|K|-|K_t|->0. Proposes the safer abstraction: Moksha = a theoretical condition of freedom from defective epistemic binding, assessed as more compatible with the mode model than a simple completeness limit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S,R,T=\text{different modes of operation} ... Rajas \rightarrow useful acquisition ... Sattva \rightarrow incorrect conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit correction against a crude reading: NOT Sattva=good knowledge, Rajas=bad knowledge, Tamas=bad knowledge. Instead S,R,T = different modes of operation (operational tendencies, not truth labels); the quality of resulting knowledge is evaluated separately. Concrete counterexamples: Rajas -> useful acquisition is possible; Sattva -> incorrect conclusion is possible if underlying evidence/model is defective; Tamas can produce a legitimate stop (insufficient evidence -> do not act).

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathbb K=(\Sigma,M,B,D,O,\delta) ... Formal Kernel Definition & Operator Algebra
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the candidate formal kernel K=(Sigma,M,B,D,O,delta) [epistemic state, operational mode, Buddhi/discrimination function, determination, admissible operations, transition function] with M in {S,R,T} and delta:(Sigma,M,O)->(Sigma',M'). Explicitly recommends stopping the addition of Gita terminology and proposes the concluding research step 'Formal Kernel Definition and Operator Algebra' with 9 questions: what is the minimum kernel state; which operations belong inside the kernel; what Buddhi formally does; how Sattva/Rajas/Tamas modify operator semantics; how Zero participates in transitions; how knowledge changes with time; which operations are internal vs external; where Governance enters without becoming part of the kernel; whether this structure can be independently derived without the Gita. Notes the source material itself cautions against selective reinterpretation, recommending every KnowledgeOS mapping be separately labelled as correspondence, hypothesis, derivation, or canonical result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operation execution \neq operation authorship
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.27's 'I am the doer' bewilderment (activities actually carried out through the modes of nature, not imported theologically): proposes Operation execution != operation authorship, decomposing Operation into intent, actor, mechanism, context, authorization, execution, result -- assessed as precisely the separation the existing provenance/authority model needs. Also, from 5.8-9's five causes of action (doer, work, situation, endeavor, fortune, not promoted as five primitives), proposes the analytical decomposition Action=f(Actor,Operation,Context,Effort,Contingency), reinforcing the principle 'do not collapse operation, actor, context, authority and outcome into one object'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operation validity \neq desired outcome
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.10-12 (relinquishing attachment to fruit): Operation validity != desired outcome -- 'the system must evaluate whether an operation was epistemically/technically justified independently of whether it produced the desired result'. Worked example: Hypothesis->Qualification->Action->Outcome=failure does not automatically mean Qualification=invalid; conversely Outcome=success does not prove Qualification=valid -- assessed as a profound connection to deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.13's city of nine gates (the self not identifying with the body's activities): proposes a kernel boundary concept distinguishing internal reasoning (state/Buddhi/qualification/transformation) from external interfaces (input/output, observation/action) -- 'the gates' understood as interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary, treated strictly as a philosophical model, not literal architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not claim that Chapter 5 solves semantic equality ... it does not provide the decision procedure for K_1\equiv K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.18's equal vision (wise person sees equally despite differences in external form): proposes NormalizePerspective(x) -- distinguish superficial representation from underlying epistemic identity, normalizing different representations before comparing underlying semantics. Explicitly and critically caveats: the Gita provides a philosophical hypothesis for why deeper equivalence matters, but does NOT provide the decision procedure for K_1 equiv K_2 (the Step 287 equality problem remains unsolved).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel invariant: discrimination should remain stable under perturbation ... d(K,x,c) \approx d(K',x,c')
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.20's sthira-buddhi (steady, unbewildered intelligence): proposes the kernel invariant that discrimination should remain stable under perturbation. Formalizes Buddhi(K,x,c)->d and proposes stability means d(K,x,c) approx d(K',x,c') under changes that are not decision-relevant -- explicitly connected to (but not identical with) the provenance/equality work. From 5.23/5.27-28, models desire, fear and anger (not literalized as human emotion) as biasing perturbations: constructs B(K,x) as a bias/perturbation function that Buddhi must discriminate from signal -- highly relevant to AI systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q(K_{t+1}) > Q(K_t) ... 100 pieces of noisy knowledge \downarrow purification \downarrow 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.11 (purification through disciplined action without attachment): sharpens purification from |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| to Q(K_{t+1})>Q(K_t) where Q is a future epistemic-quality function. Concrete illustration: a kernel could transform 100 pieces of noisy knowledge into 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge, becoming better despite becoming smaller -- assessed as a major correction to a purely information-quantity model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Kernel State ... A kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit separation: Knowledge State K_t answers 'what does the system currently represent/know', Kernel State (fraktur K)_t = (K_t,M_t,B_t,Z_t,Pi_t) answers 'in what condition is the system currently processing that knowledge'. K_t != (fraktur K)_t: a kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode, or hold incomplete knowledge with excellent discrimination/qualification behaviour -- assessed as very important for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model. Candidate kernel transition: (fraktur K)_t --Buddhi--> o_t --Purify--> (fraktur K)_{t+1}. Final consolidated formula: K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))). Concluding principle: the Kernel is not the Knowledge; the Kernel is the smallest active unit that operates on Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Inference asks what can we conclude from what we know. Step 34 asks What should we learn next? ... a fundamentally different problem
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference from information-acquisition selection as fundamentally different problems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 10^6 uncertain assertions ... impossible and unnecessary to validate all of them immediately ... Choose the information acquisition action that produces the greatest useful improvement relative to its cost
a_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS should not investigate everything, requiring a cost-relative optimization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cost(I) ... Time, Money, Compute, HumanAttention, OperationalRisk ... information is not free

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI=L_0-L_{PI} ... an upper bound on the value of information

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=L_0-E_Y[\min_d E[L(d,\theta)\mid K,Y]] ... NVOI(I)=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) ... the core mathematical idea
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Sample Information and net value of information as the step's core idea.

a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first formal Next-Best-Epistemic-Action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: InformationValue\neq UncertaintyReduction ... A has no influence on any important decision ... UncertaintyReduction(A) may have almost zero practical value
a_rows_sample.statement: States the subtle principle that information value is not the same as uncertainty reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionSensitivity(A,D) ... Information about A is valuable if learning A can change d^*
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines DecisionSensitivity as the criterion for information value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus has 31 GB RAM ... migration architecture does not depend on RAM beyond a very large safety margin ... almost no decision value
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of low-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (RAM precision beyond safety margin).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Production database backup is restorable ... DecisionSensitivity(B,D) is very high ... validating B may have extremely high VOI
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting example of high-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (backup restorability).

a_rows_sample.anchor: d^*=f(K) ... If perturbing A does not change f(K), then A has low local decision sensitivity
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a decision-relevance partition via perturbation of the decision function.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(A) ... A\rightarrow B\rightarrow D ... DependencyClosure+DecisionCriticality=EpistemicPrioritization
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines Step 32's dependency closure with decision dependency, giving a prioritization formula.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(D) ... Low, Medium, High, Critical ... should be domain-owned. KnowledgeOS can consume it but should not invent the business meaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a domain-owned Criticality classification, not invented by KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EL(d)=E[L(d,\theta)\mid K] ... d^*=\arg\min_d EL(d) ... d_1 expected loss 10, d_2 expected loss 12 ... investigation may reveal a high-risk state in which d_2 becomes preferable
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected loss and current-optimal decision, worked with a two-decision expected-loss-reversal example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Risk<5\%\Rightarrow AutomaticApproval ... Risk\in[3\%,8\%] ... DecisionBoundaryUncertainty. Uncertainty far from a decision boundary may be harmless. Uncertainty near a boundary can be critical
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DecisionBoundaryUncertainty, worked with a threshold-straddling risk-interval example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Risk\in[1\%,2\%] ... no urgent investigation ... Risk\in[4\%,7\%] crosses the decision boundary ... additional evidence is valuable
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting examples of harmless-far and critical-boundary-straddling risk intervals.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(A)\propto DecisionImpact(A)\times Uncertainty(A) ... conceptual, not yet a universal formula
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual, not-yet-universal epistemic-triage priority formula.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=10, Cost(I)=2, NVOI(I)=8 ... EVSI=12, Cost=20, NVOI=-8 ... should not be prioritized merely because it provides more information
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked arithmetic example showing higher-EVSI investigations can have lower net value once cost is subtracted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HumanAttention is an epistemic resource ... 2 hours of a senior architect's time may be more expensive than a machine-readable check
a_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is itself a costed epistemic resource, worked with a comparison example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence_total = Confidence_1 x Confidence_2 x Confidence_3 ... That is generally wrong
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects naive multiplication of stage confidences as generally wrong; the correct propagation depends on uncertainty semantics and dependence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Measurement uncertainty, Sampling uncertainty, Parameter uncertainty, Model uncertainty, Prediction uncertainty, Epistemic uncertainty, Aleatory variability ... must not automatically be collapsed into one number
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes at least seven kinds of uncertainty that must not be collapsed into one number.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Aleatory variability: Variation inherent in the phenomenon ... Epistemic uncertainty: Uncertainty caused by incomplete knowledge ... Randomness != LackOfKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the aleatory-vs-epistemic distinction with a travel-time/traffic example, giving the principle Randomness != LackOfKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=X+epsilon ... E[epsilon]=0 and Var(epsilon)=sigma^2 ... those assumptions themselves require justification
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a basic measurement-error model and warns its moment assumptions require justification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=h(X,theta,epsilon) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the measurement model where available
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes to a measurement model KnowledgeOS should preserve, else downstream models may treat measured values as exact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Var(Y) approx J Sigma J^T ... Jacobian ... covariance matrix ... exposes why independent multiplication of confidence values is inadequate
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes first-order error propagation via the Jacobian and covariance matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cov(X_i,X_j) != 0 ... Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y)+2Cov(X,Y) ... Dependence matters
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes covariance's role in propagation, giving the principle that dependence matters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 and E_2 both come from the same underlying report. Treating them as independent could artificially increase certainty. This is a major risk in AI systems
b_rows_sample.statement: States the evidence-duplication problem as a major risk in AI systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1=f(S), E_2=g(S) ... E_1 not-perp E_2 ... combining them as independent evidence is invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes correlated evidence sharing a common source and invalidates treating it as independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance -> DependenceStructure -> CorrectUncertaintyPropagation ... This is a major result
b_rows_sample.statement: States provenance's mathematical role: it enables estimating dependency and hence correct uncertainty propagation, called a major result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H)/P(E) ... prior P(H) and likelihood P(E|H) must have explicit provenance and assumptions
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Bayesian updating and requires explicit provenance/assumptions for prior and likelihood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not every knowledge problem has a meaningful prior ... BayesianUpdate must be a typed operation requiring a valid probabilistic model. It should not be the universal inference engine
b_rows_sample.statement: Constrains Bayesian updating to be a typed operation requiring a valid model, not a universal inference engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: confidence intervals; sampling distributions; hypothesis tests; bootstrap distributions; asymptotic approximations ... theta-hat +- z SE(theta-hat) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the framework
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists frequentist uncertainty representations and requires preserving the inferential framework used.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A standard confidence interval [L,U] should not automatically be interpreted as P(L<=theta<=U)=0.95. That interpretation is generally Bayesian, not classical frequentist
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against the common misinterpretation of a frequentist confidence interval as a Bayesian probability statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [L,U] ... Latency in [100ms,150ms] ... No probability distribution is required
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines interval uncertainty requiring no probability distribution, with a latency example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in S where S is a feasible set ... useful when evidence constrains the possibilities without assigning probabilities
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes interval uncertainty to set-valued uncertainty over a feasible set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [0,100] but have no justified distribution. The system should not invent X~Uniform(0,100) ... Bounded != Probabilistically Specified
b_rows_sample.statement: Forbids inventing a uniform distribution over a bounded but unjustified range, giving the principle Bounded != Probabilistically Specified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: theta in Theta_I ... PartiallyIdentified. This is stronger than simply saying uncertain
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces partial identification as a distinct, stronger-than-generic-uncertainty statistical concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10<=X<=20 and Y=2X ... 20<=Y<=40 ... propagated a set-valued constraint without inventing a probability distribution
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of set-valued constraint propagation without inventing a distribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_1,X_2 -> Y -> Z ... KnowledgeOS should preserve DependencyGraph. Then uncertainty can be propagated through the graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a dependency graph structure for propagating uncertainty through a network.

b_aliases: Uncertainty Propagation, Dependence, Correlation, Error Propagation and Epistemic Risk

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(A,R) is sufficient IFF the mandatory operation set excludes every history-sensitive predicate. ever_contested is not an exotic operation ... 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient knowledge state' is not a theorem of the corpus. It is a consequence of an unstated choice of O, and a different, equally corpus-consistent O refutes it. This is the sharpest form of EV-E1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding KG-4 (EXP-3): constructs two histories (H_calm: a single assert; H_stormy: assert, contradicting assert, relate as contradicts, withdraw) that reach a byte-identical K=(A,R) yet differ on ever_contested(H) (False vs True); since ever_contested is an ordinary governance predicate discussed in the corpus's own Steps 155/179/181, this refutes 'K=(A,R) is minimal and sufficient' as a corpus theorem, showing it holds only conditionally on excluding history-sensitive predicates from the mandatory operation set -- described as the sharpest form of finding EV-E1 (from the prior batch's independent theory-evolution reconstruction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The transformation is well-behaved RELATIVE TO a four-operation set this session chose. Every corpus property that quantifies over T ... is UNDERDETERMINED until O is enumerated ... Add one history-sensitive operation ... and K=(A,R) stops being sufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding TG-5: the executable kernel's good properties (TG-4) hold only relative to the specific four-operation set chosen for this session; every corpus property quantifying over the operation set (sufficiency Step 259, congruence Step 260.9, minimality Steps 260/266.19, state equality) is underdetermined until the set is fixed, and exp_congruence.py EXP-3 shows the sufficiency answer actually flips once an ordinary governance-plausible history-sensitive operation (ever_contested) is added, even though it does not appear in the chosen minimal or full operation sets tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F-1 -- The minimality claim is conditional, not false ... Whether K=(A,R) suffices depends entirely on whether O contains such a predicate, and O has never been written down. The corpus's terminal claim is TRUE RELATIVE TO A PREMISE IT NEVER STATES. That is a different and more repairable failure than being wrong.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding FR-3 (one of 'the three refutations that matter most'): reframes the K=(A,R)-minimality refutation as the claim being underdetermined rather than false -- it is true relative to an unstated premise (a fixed operation set O excluding history-sensitive predicates like ever_contested), which is characterized as a different and more repairable kind of failure than an outright false claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Treat Knowledge Space as a measurable space, and treat a knowledge projection as a measure. ... Five distinct mathematical objections, each correct: A proposition is not a subset of Ω. e∈𝓕 is a type error. ... Confidence, relevance, stability, attention are not countably additive ... ∇·J requires ge
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces ARC A (measure theory): the original 2026-08-25 proposal to treat knowledge as a measurable space/projection-as-measure was refuted just seven minutes later by five correct mathematical objections (a proposition is not a subset of the sample space; confidence/relevance/stability/attention are not countably additive so are not measures; the divergence PDE needs geometry the bare measurable space lacks; TV/Wasserstein/JS/KL divergences are not interchangeable; the Alignment=1-distance formula is invalid across different distance ranges) — all independently verified correct by this session.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω = all possible knowledge states collapses the domain space and the epistemic state space ... A filtration is not knowledge. ... Conditional expectation E[X_t|𝓕_t^A] is the filtering regime's projection, not the universal one — and it presupposes an X_t that KnowledgeOS has never defined. ... marti
b_rows_sample.statement: A second, six-part round of category errors (found the same day) further dismantled a stochastic-filtering reformulation of knowledge: conflating the domain and epistemic state spaces, treating a filtration as knowledge itself, presupposing an undefined X_t inside a conditional expectation, conflating differing information with differing probability measures across agents, misreading Radon-Nikodym incomparability as epistemic incomparability, and mistaking specific stochastic-process properties (martingale, submartingale, quadratic variation, Ito SDEs) for general epistemic properties (stability, learning, noise, evolution law).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemology/Semantics → Measurable structure → Measurement ... the kernel preserves substrate, not derived mathematics: KOS_core=(Identity, Participants, Context, Boundary, Time, Observations, Relations, Provenance, History, Transitions, AccessScope, RegimeReferences) ... Measure theory becomes one
b_rows_sample.statement: The repaired ARC-A model (established 2026-08-25 ~19:00) externalizes measure theory entirely: the kernel preserves only a domain-agnostic substrate (KOS_core, a twelve-field tuple including Provenance, History, Transitions, RegimeReferences), with probabilistic, logical, causal, statistical and other regimes all treated as pluggable, non-foundational add-ons.
