b_rows_sample.statement: ARC B census: an exhaustive grep of the entire primary corpus finds roughly 28 distinct, mutually incompatible right-hand-side definitions of K, spanning seven fundamentally different mathematical KINDS (set-with-relations, labelled graph, flat record, subset of a universe, measurable space, a single justified proposition — a category error relative to the rest — and a state/history pair), with no morphism between kinds ever stated anywhere in the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Finding EV-B1 (EXECUTED). Three of the incompatible tuples (#4, #5, #6) occur in one file (20260826-161551), and three more (#8, #9, #10) occur in Q14 alone. The instability is not only across the corpus's history; it is within single documents. A contradiction registry organized by step cannot see
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-B1: K's instability is not only chronological — three incompatible K definitions occur within a single file (20260826-161551), and three more occur within Q14 alone, meaning a contradiction registry organized only by step number is structurally blind to this within-document instability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-B3 (DERIVED). The terminal form K=(𝒜,ℛ) is strictly poorer than #8 and #9. Q6's (𝒜,ℛ,ℰ,ℋ,𝒵,ℒ) carries evidence, history, zero and lineage as first-class components; (𝒜,ℛ) carries neither evidence nor history nor status. ... The corpus arrived at its smallest K by relocating components, but the re
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-B3, directly qualifying the K=(A,R) minimality narrative used throughout this batch: the terminal K=(A,R) is strictly poorer in stated components than earlier Q6/Q13 candidates (which carried evidence, history, zero-findings and lineage as first-class parts of K itself); the reduction to (A,R) worked by relocating those components elsewhere (into Assertion internals, external History, external Policy), but the relocation targets were fixed AFTER the reduction rather than justified before it, and whether (A,R) is actually SUFFICIENT is exactly the still-open Step 259/260 congruence question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ARC B: UNRESOLVED. The corpus's own verdict (Step 240) and this session's independent census agree. This is not inherited: the census was run before the registry was read.
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC B (what is K) is classified UNRESOLVED, with the corpus's own Step 240 Contradiction Registry (which independently found 'approximately 25 materially different right-hand sides' and explicitly refused to retroactively call them all projections without demonstration) agreeing with this session's independently-run census — the agreement is genuine since the census was run before the registry was consulted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence is not a property of a document. Evidence(O,P,C,R) — observation O is evidence for proposition P under context C and evaluation rule R. ... the observation 'the server returned 3.69' is evidence for P1 but not for P2 ('Nexus is secure') nor P3. Hence Evidence(O,P1) ≠ Evidence(O,P2); evidenc
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC C: the corpus's relational Evidence(O,P,C,R) model (evidence is never a property of a document alone, but relative to a specific proposition under context and rule) is independently checked against a concrete counterexample and accepted as a sound, genuine argument, not a mere assertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-C1 (DERIVED, HIGH). ... Step 266 independently classifies Relevant(A) as Class C — not computable as currently defined ... the qualification rule exists and is well-formed; its load-bearing predicate is undecidable as specified. These two results live 3 days and 240 steps apart and are never brou
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-C1: the corpus's evidence-qualification rule (relevance to a proposition under an explicit rule) and its own later computability audit (Step 266, classifying Relevant(A) as non-computable as currently specified) are logically connected — the qualification rule's load-bearing predicate is exactly the one later shown undecidable — yet no document anywhere in the 270-step, 3-day-separated corpus ever connects these two results, so 'evidence is closed' (Closure-04) and 'relevance is open' (Step 266) coexist unreconciled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admission is not a truth function. An assertion may be admitted into K while being weak, contested or wrong ... EpistemicStatus ⊥ GovernanceStatus ... Separation: CORPUS ESTABLISHES | Vocabulary: UNRESOLVED. Superseded, Invalidated, Contested and Conflicted are each assigned to different axes in dif
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC D: the Epistemic-Status/Governance-Status orthogonality is confirmed CORPUS ESTABLISHES (admission is not a truth function; an assertion can be admitted while weak/contested/wrong), but the actual vocabulary membership remains UNRESOLVED — terms like Superseded, Invalidated, Contested, and Conflicted are inconsistently assigned to one axis or the other across different corpus documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic minimality ≠ syntactic compactness. ... ≡ must be a congruence for 𝒯, not just an equivalence relation. DERIVED, and correctly so. Reflexivity PROVISIONALLY DERIVED ... symmetry and transitivity DERIVED under ordinary equality. This session checked the three proofs: they are correct but tri
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC E (State vs History, called 'the deepest and most honest arc') is independently checked and found genuinely sound where claimed: semantic minimality is correctly distinguished from mere syntactic compactness; the requirement that the equivalence relation be a congruence (not merely an equivalence) for the transformation set is correctly derived; the reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity proofs are verified correct but trivial (holding for any observational equivalence, establishing nothing KnowledgeOS-specific) — and importantly, the corpus itself does not overclaim them; hash identity is correctly kept distinct from semantic identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-E1 (DERIVED, CRITICAL). Step 260.16: membership requires the equivalence test — H∈[H₀] ⟺ H≡H₀. Step 260.9: ≡ quantifies over the whole transformation algebra 𝒯. Step 266: 𝒯 is not closed. Therefore ≡ is defined by a universal quantification over a set that has never been enumerated. It is not mer
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-E1 (CRITICAL), sharper than the corpus's own Step 260 gate: since the semantic-equivalence relation equiv is defined by universal quantification over the mandatory transformation algebra T, and T itself is not closed/fully enumerated (per Step 266), equiv is not merely undecidable — it is NOT YET A WELL-DEFINED RELATION, because its defining quantifier ranges over an open, unenumerated collection; every object depending on it (the minimal quotient K*, membership A in K, state equality K1=K2, and the Step 259 sufficiency/congruence theorem) inherits this indeterminacy, undermining the confidence level of the congruence-based results relied on throughout the batch's canonical-K work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F1 Lens-driven pre-1…~158 ... F2 Formal build-out 001…215 ... F3 Archaeology & audit 213…270 the corpus turns on itself: evidence ledger, concept genealogy, contradiction registry, minimality, computability, empirical bridge, adversarial audit. ... The regime shift at ~Step 213 is the corpus's most
b_rows_sample.statement: ARC F identifies three successive method regimes across the corpus's history: F1 lens-driven (philosophical/scriptural lenses through step ~158), F2 formal build-out (algebras, type systems, architecture through step 215), and F3 archaeology-and-audit (the corpus turning on itself, steps 213-270) — the F1-to-F3 transition is self-diagnosed within the corpus itself, at step 236, explicitly titled 'We Have a Problem With the Existing Reconstruction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EV-F2 (EXECUTED, CRITICAL). F3 audits by reading, never by running. Across all 270 steps and 550 files there are zero executable artifacts (INV-9). Steps titled 'Executable Knowledge State Model', 'Property-Based Falsification', 'Adversarial End-to-End Simulation', 'Executable Reference Model', and
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding EV-F2 (CRITICAL): despite five step titles explicitly claiming to build and run executable/simulation models, the 270-step, 550-file numbered corpus contains ZERO actual executable artifacts — each such step contains only prose narrating what a hypothetical program would report; the only genuine Python files anywhere in the corpus were written by a separate, later review session (not the step-corpus itself) and cover only three specific claims out of several hundred made across the programme — directly explaining why the corpus could never run its own nominated strongest empirical test (EV-A1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: None of these findings is a claim that the corpus is dishonest. ARCs A, D and E in particular contain mathematics of real quality, and Steps 240, 255, 260, 266 and 267 state their own negative results plainly. The findings are about what the corpus's method could not reach: it could not execute, and
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing methodological caveat: none of the EV findings allege dishonesty — several arcs (A, D, E) contain genuinely high-quality mathematics, and the corpus itself plainly states several of its own negative results (Steps 240, 255, 260, 266, 267); the findings instead characterize a structural limit of the corpus's method — it could never execute code, and after step 258 it could no longer check itself against a genuinely independent second source.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Purpose: produce EXECUTED evidence where the corpus has only PROSE. Nothing here is architecture. Nothing here is authoritative. It is a witness. The kernel implements the corpus's TERMINAL formal model, taken from Steps 262/263/265/267/269.
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel's stated purpose is explicitly to produce EXECUTED evidence where the corpus itself has only prose, and it explicitly disclaims any authoritative or architectural status for itself, calling itself merely 'a witness' — directly operationalizing the theory-evolution-map's EV-F2 critique that the numbered-step corpus never actually runs code.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H3 is UNDECIDED, and H4 is CONFIRMED: K=(A,R) is sufficient IFF the mandatory operation set O excludes every history-sensitive predicate. The corpus never closes O (Step 266: the operation registry is missing; policy and authority are class-C). Therefore 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient state' is
b_rows_sample.statement: Final conclusion of the executable experiment set: H3 (K=(A,R) is a sufficient history abstraction) is left UNDECIDED and H4 (this session's EV-E1 claim) is CONFIRMED by execution — K=(A,R)'s sufficiency holds if and only if the mandatory operation set excludes every history-sensitive predicate, and since the corpus never actually closes that operation set (Step 266 leaves the operation registry incomplete and policy/authority non-computable as specified), the widely-repeated claim 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient state' is explicitly judged NOT a theorem of the corpus but merely a consequence of an unstated choice of the operation set O.

a_notations: K=(A,R) sufficient iff O excludes history-sensitive predicates

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'k-sufficiency-conditional-on-unstated-operation-set' POSSIBLY relates to 'theory-evolution-map-independent-reconstruction' (batch B0041). Note: Executed demonstration (exp_congruence.py EXP-3) that two histories with different contestation trajectories (H_calm vs H_stormy) reach a byte-identical K=(A,R), so K is sufficient only if the mandatory operation set excludes history-sensitive predicates like ever_contested (an ordinary governance predicate the corpus's own Steps 155/179/181 discuss); concludes the widely-repeated claim 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient knowledge state' is not a corpus theorem but a consequence of an unstated choice of O.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R5 drop timestamps 0.0000 0 YES; R4 round to 3 s.f. 0.4299 35,532 NO; R3 round to 2 s.f. 0.8546 246,235 NO; R2 rank 3.3937 5,530,777 NO
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 result table across the chain D->R5->R4->R3->R2: R5 (drop timestamps) is empirically adequate (Hhat(Q|R)=0, N_viol=0); R4 (round to 3 s.f.), R3 (round to 2 s.f.), and R2 (rank) are each inadequate with increasing Hhat(Q|R) and N_viol; identifies the first preservation boundary as R5->R4 caused by T4 (rounding to 3 significant digits), but insists the correct scientific statement is scoped to 'for the specified carrier, inquiry Q, contract Pi, transformation chain, and value alphabet V=12, R5 was empirically adequate and R4 was empirically inadequate' rather than a general claim that three significant digits is a universal preservation limit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R4 = T4(R5); R3 = T3(R4); R2 = T2(R3) ... data-processing inequality gives H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n) ... adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives, via the data-processing inequality applied to the deterministic chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} (each R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n)), that H(Q|R_5)<=H(Q|R_4)<=H(Q|R_3)<=H(Q|R_2), i.e. adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain; reclassifies the original hypothesis H-C (that adequacy could become non-monotone, e.g. R3 adequate again after R4 inadequate) not as empirically falsified by the data but as structurally ill-posed/a priori inapplicable to this experiment class, recommending the frozen label read '[THEORY/NEG] H-C was ill-posed for the specified sequential deterministic chain; the data-processing inequality makes non-monotone conditional-entropy adequacy impossible' rather than 'H-C refuted a priori', on the ground that a priori impossibility and empirical falsification are epistemically distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential family: D -> R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 ... No recovery is possible. Parallel family: D -> R_A, D -> R_B, D -> R_C ... Non-monotone comparative behavior is possible here.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a distinction proposed to become part of the theory: a 'sequential family' of representations (each derived deterministically from the previous one) where H(Q|R) is provably monotone with no recovery possible, versus a 'parallel family' of independently constructed representations from the same source D, where one representation can destroy a distinction while another independently preserves it, so non-monotone comparative adequacy is possible; frames this as the difference between monotonicity along a sequential information-reducing chain and comparative adequacy across independently constructed representations, expected to matter when investigating alternative knowledge representations later.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hhat(Q)=5.0098 ... R5=15.042, R4=12.307, R3=11.097, R2=7.170 ... Hhat(R_n) > Hhat(Q) at every level ... empirical consistency with the theoretical bound.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-E's result that empirical Hhat(R_n) exceeds Hhat(Q) at every level of the chain (R5=15.042 through R2=7.170, versus Hhat(Q)=5.0098), matching the expected theoretical lower-bound relationship under the relevant assumptions, and endorses treating this as empirical consistency with the theoretical bound rather than as a proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R5 -> R4 Zero rate 3.77% / R4 -> R3 Zero rate 4.26% / R3 -> R2 Zero rate 0.00% ... does not show a Zero/boundary relationship ... we should not make Zero the fundamental preservation criterion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports hypothesis H-RR2's negative result: measured Zero rates across the chain (3.77%, 4.26%, 0.00%) show no association between Zero and the observed preservation boundary, refuting the original suspicion that Zero -> preservation boundary; concludes Zero should not be treated as the fundamental preservation criterion but as one possible mechanism within a broader architecture that separately includes eliminability/Zero, preservation/adequacy, realization, and reduction cost.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE -> Transformation / Representation / Inquiry Q / Preservation contract Pi / Decoder O -> Recoverability/Adequacy -> Preservation boundary -> Eliminability(Zero) / Reduction measures
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a revised overall theory architecture diagram superseding the prior linear trajectory (Vedic transformations -> Zero/eliminability -> relationality -> representation reduction -> preservation): SOURCE branches into Transformation, Representation, Inquiry Q, Preservation contract Pi, and Decoder O, which jointly determine Recoverability/Adequacy, which locates a Preservation boundary, which in turn splits into Eliminability (Zero) and Reduction measures as two downstream, non-foundational consequences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Mathematical theory: H(Q|R)=0 ... H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) ... R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) => H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). B. KR-ZERO empirical evidence [list]. C. KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical evidence [list].
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the current state of knowledge into three tiers: (A) the mathematical theory -- H(Q|R)=0 as the sufficiency/adequacy criterion, the decomposition H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) for adequate deterministic representations, and the monotonicity consequence H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n); (B) a nine-point list of KR-ZERO empirical findings (Zero is context/transformation/contract-relative, group Zero can differ from member Zero, higher-order determination exists but is not universal, interaction order is not globally monotonic, the phenomenon is transformation-dependent, Zero gives no simple universal kernel/algebra); (C) a ten-point list of KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical findings (observable preservation boundary in a sequential chain, boundary detectable via Q-recoverability, first loss at T4 in this run, reduction is multidimensional, adequacy and realization can diverge, a purely representational recoding can leave recoverability unchanged while altering a fixed decoder, Zero did not correlate with the boundary, contract failure and operator-only failure did not occur, non-monotone adequacy was structurally impossible for this chain).

b_rows_sample.anchor: At which transformation does the representation cease to preserve the inquiry we care about? ... Given inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi, does representation R still contain enough information to recover Q? ... a potentially powerful foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the practical KnowledgeOS payoff of the representation-reduction results: given a progressive construction chain from raw document through structured representation, claims, relations, normalized claims, knowledge representation, to compressed knowledge representation, the rigorous question 'at which transformation does the representation cease to preserve inquiry Q' can be answered by measuring H(Q|R_n), N_viol(R_n), H(R_n|Q), and representation cost -- proposed as a more rigorous foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine than an informal judgment that summarized information 'still looks present'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We currently have THEORY + preservation/adequacy mathematics + KR-ZERO empirical constraints + KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical demonstration. We do NOT yet have a general knowledge extraction calculus, because we have only tested a deliberately small numerical carrier r=(value, source, timestamp) with Q=
b_rows_sample.statement: States explicitly that the current results do not amount to a general knowledge-extraction theory: they were tested only on a small numerical carrier r=(value, source, timestamp) with a specific Q=(argmax_source, decile(total)) and one particular transformation chain, and transferring the theory to richer carriers (documents, claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal states, evidence) remains an open research question, characterized as 'perfectly fine' rather than a defect.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The next thing I would not do is immediately write Theory v1.3. I would first perform a results audit of the actual KR-REP-REDUCTION corpus/metrics and implementation, especially checking the exact definitions of C, empirical entropy vs Miller-Madow entropy, rank ties, and the R5->R4 boundary counts
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends against immediately writing a Theory v1.3 revision and instead calls for a results audit of the actual KR-REP-REDUCTION corpus, metrics, and implementation first -- specifically checking the exact definition of the admissibility constraint C, empirical entropy versus Miller-Madow entropy estimation, handling of rank ties, and the R5->R4 boundary counts -- with theory revision to follow only if those survive audit; this recommendation directly foreshadows the subsequent corpus/theory audit work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Old KR-ZERO result: KEEP / FREEZE, with the mechanistic wording narrowed ... New KR-REP-REDUCTION result: ACCEPT as a successful first representation-reduction experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an overall verdict: keep/freeze the old KR-ZERO result (with mechanistic wording narrowed) whose major contribution is that eliminability can be relational, contextual, transformation-dependent, and sometimes higher-order; accept the new KR-REP-REDUCTION result as a successful first representation-reduction experiment whose major contributions are that a specified representation chain can be experimentally tested for preservation with a boundary located without assuming it in advance, that adequacy (what a representation makes recoverable) is distinct from realization (what a particular decoder actually recovers), and that sequential reduction and parallel representation comparison are different mathematical regimes that should become a permanent theoretical distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment demonstrates contract-relative recoverability loss under a deterministic sequential representation chain. ... The document itself appropriately restricts the preservation-boundary claim to the specified carrier, inquiry, contract, transformation chain, and alphabet.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 headline claim: the key result is not yet 'representation reduction' but more precisely that the experiment demonstrates contract-relative recoverability loss under a deterministic sequential representation chain D->R5->R4->R3->R2, with the preservation-boundary claim properly restricted to the specified carrier, inquiry, contract, transformation chain, and value alphabet.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n ... H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n) ... Once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream. [THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint. [NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives from R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) with deterministic T_n that H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), boxing the consequence 'once sufficiency is lost in this chain, it cannot be recovered downstream', and formally classifies this as '[THEORY] Sequential data-processing constraint' with the accompanying '[NEG] H-C is structurally inapplicable to deterministic sequential reduction' rather than retaining H-C as an empirical hypothesis for this experiment class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential reduction: D->R5->R4->R3->R2 ... information sufficiency is monotone. Parallel alternatives: D-> R_A/R_B/R_C ... H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible ... we should preserve it permanently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes and endorses permanently preserving the distinction between Sequential Reduction (D->R5->R4->R3->R2, where information sufficiency is monotone by data processing) and Alternative/Parallel Representation Comparison (D branching into R_A, R_B, R_C with no data-processing ordering between them, so H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible), naming these two distinct research regimes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Representation != Recoverability != Realization, where Representation = what is encoded; Recoverability = what can in principle be reconstructed; Realization = what a particular decoder actually reconstructs.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a three-way conceptual distinction -- Representation (what is encoded), Recoverability (what can in principle be reconstructed), and Realization (what a particular decoder actually reconstructs) -- as strictly non-identical properties, proposed to become a major concept in the future KnowledgeOS extraction architecture, sharper than a mere two-way adequacy-vs-realization split.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_up =~enc R_down if and only if the implementation demonstrates a bijection between them ... exists f,g: f(R_up)=R_down, g(R_down)=R_up with g o f = id, f o g = id. Only then should we connect this experiment strongly to the existing Q-equivalence research.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that the ascending/descending rank representations only be called equivalent (R_up cong_enc R_down) once the implementation demonstrates an actual bijection f,g between them satisfying g.f=id and f.g=id, and that any residual measured difference in H(Q|R) absent such a bijection be attributed to sampling/estimation or implementation effects rather than treated as evidence of non-equivalence; only a confirmed bijection should connect this result to the existing Q-equivalence research.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero -> PreservationBoundary. The experiment did not demonstrate that. ... Zero != definition of preservation ... This is good news, because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular: Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that the negative finding Zero != definition of preservation (observed Zero rates 3.77%, 4.26%, 0% showing no demonstrated correspondence with the R5->R4 preservation boundary) is good news because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular (Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation), providing evidence that Zero, preservation, realization, and reduction are separate research concerns.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (D,Q,Pi) -> R -> {Adequacy, Realization, Eliminability, Cost}. This is significantly better than trying to make Zero the central algebra from which everything else follows.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a cleaner research architecture where (D,Q,Pi) determines a representation R, which is then evaluated along four independent axes -- Adequacy, Realization, Eliminability, Cost -- explicitly rejecting the earlier framing that tried to make Zero the central algebra from which everything else follows.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The tested carrier is still very small: r=(value,source,timestamp) ... We have not yet demonstrated preservation over semantic claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal claims, evidence, hypotheses, epistemic standards. So the proper abstraction is currently Contract-relative
b_rows_sample.statement: Insists the current abstraction be called 'contract-relative representation preservation', not 'knowledge extraction calculus', because the tested carrier remains a small numerical tuple r=(value,source,timestamp) and preservation has not yet been demonstrated over semantic claims, entities, relations, provenance, contradictions, temporal claims, evidence, hypotheses, or epistemic standards.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The next audit should explicitly test target leakage. Q not-in Inputs(T), Q not-in Inputs(O), Q not-in Inputs(C), except for the evaluator. ... D --T--> R --O--> Qhat ... evaluator independently computes Q(D). Then compare Qhat =? Q(D).
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new required audit check for target leakage: the inquiry target Q must not appear in the inputs of the transformation T, the decoder O, or the constraint C except as the evaluator's independent target, specifying the clean experimental architecture D--T-->R--O-->Qhat with an evaluator independently computing Q(D) and comparing Qhat against Q(D), to guard against the answer being indirectly encoded into the transformation or decoder.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now consolidate the previous experiments. The objective is to identify the smallest set of invariants whose violation would fundamentally change the nature of KnowledgeOS. Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity+DeterministicVerification+Traceability+Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 120's objective: identifying the smallest invariant set whose violation would fundamentally change KnowledgeOS, starting from a seven-part candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.1 — What makes an invariant constitutional? A constitutional invariant says: if this property is violated, the system no longer has the intended semantic character. ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention. 'Use PostgreSQL' is not necessarily constitutional. 'Authoritative knowledge must have id
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention: a constitutional invariant's violation changes the system's intended semantic character, illustrated by contrasting a technology preference with a provenance requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.2 — Invariant K1: Provenance ... Every authoritative knowledge object MUST have provenance. Provenance should answer where did it originate, when, through which process, who/what produced it, from which source material.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K1: every authoritative knowledge object must have provenance answering five questions (origin/when/process/producer/source material).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.4 — Experiment K1.1 ... KnowledgeOS contains 'The architecture requires rootless containers.' No source, author, decision, timestamp or provenance exists. Can the system establish that it is authoritative? No. Verdict: K1 VIOLATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K1.1: a sourceless/authorless/timestampless architecture statement cannot be established as authoritative; verdict K1 VIOLATED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.5 — Provenance does not equal source URL ... SourceURL does not tell us WhoApproved or WhenDidItBecomeValid. Source≠CompleteProvenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Source≠CompleteProvenance: a URL alone does not establish approval or validity onset.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.6 — Invariant K2: Authority ... Every authoritative governance change MUST have identifiable authority. Decision→Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K2: every authoritative governance change must have identifiable authority (Decision->Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.8 — Experiment K2.1 ... Agent generates 'Architecture standard changed to X.' No authorized decision exists. Expected: Status=Proposed. Not Status=Authoritative. Verdict: K2 VIOLATION if promoted
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K2.1: an unauthorized agent-declared standard change must remain Status=Proposed; K2 VIOLATION if promoted to Authoritative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.9 — Authority is not identity ... Actor≠Authority. Credential≠Authority. Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly establishes the mapping.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Actor≠Authority, Credential≠Authority, Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly maps them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.10 — Invariant K3: Epistemic status ... KnowledgeOS MUST distinguish observed, verified, inferred, proposed and authoritative information. This is perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K3, called perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant: distinguishing observed/verified/inferred/proposed/authoritative information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.12 — Experiment K3.1 ... LLM generates Inference(X). System stores it identically to AuthoritativeDecision(X). Expected: K3 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K3.1: storing an LLM inference identically to an authoritative decision is K3 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.13 — Candidate epistemic states ... Observed, Imported, Asserted, Inferred, Proposed, Verified, Approved, Superseded. But we should only implement states that have real semantic value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eight-value candidate epistemic vocabulary, cautioning only states with real semantic value should be implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.14 — Invariant K4: Temporal validity ... Authoritative knowledge MUST have determinable temporal validity. At minimum Current versus Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K4: authoritative knowledge must have determinable temporal validity, at minimum Current vs Superseded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.16 — Experiment K4.1 ... Two decisions exist: D1 use architecture A, D2 use architecture B. No relationship identifies which supersedes which. Expected: agent cannot safely determine current architecture. Verdict: K4 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.1: two competing, unlinked decisions leave an agent unable to safely determine current architecture; verdict K4 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.17 — Creation time versus validity ... We must explicitly distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. And potentially ValidUntil.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt must be distinguished from ValidFrom (and potentially ValidUntil).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.18 — Experiment K4.2 ... Decision created 2026-08-01 but effective 2026-09-01. If the system only knows created_at, it cannot correctly answer is this decision currently effective. Verdict: K4 PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.2: a decision created before its effective date cannot be correctly evaluated by a created_at-only system; verdict K4 PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.19 — Invariant K5: Deterministic verification ... Where a claim is deterministically testable, authoritative assurance MUST be based on reproducible verification evidence. This does not eliminate human judgment. It prevents LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K5: deterministically testable claims must be assured via reproducible evidence, preventing LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim → Locate → Inspect → Trace → Test → Observe → Classify → Report
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EEP = {E1..E8}: an eight-stage mandatory pipeline (Claim, Locate, Inspect, Trace, Test, Observe, Classify, Report) that an agent must explicitly state it performed (not necessarily at equal depth) before making an architectural claim; the governing principle is 'an agent must prove an architectural claim from evidence; it must not prove it from plausibility.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural / Behavioral / Governance / Temporal / Assurance / Operational
b_rows_sample.statement: E1 Claim requires a precise, falsifiable proposition (contrasts 'Understand KnowledgeOS' [bad] with a typed claim like 'AuthoritativeDecision -> Provenance' [good]) and distinguishes six claim types: Structural (component depends on component), Behavioral (creating an authoritative object requires provenance), Governance (only an authorized actor can approve), Temporal (superseded decisions excluded from current knowledge), Assurance (rule X deterministically verified), Operational (runtime state fed back into KnowledgeOS).

b_rows_sample.anchor: NotFound(Location) ≠ Absent(System)
b_rows_sample.statement: E2 Locate names search targets (README, docs/, ADR/, architecture/, src/, tests/, schemas/, migrations/, config/, CI/CD, hooks/, agents/, runtime configuration) and states the negative-evidence rule: finding nothing in one location does not prove system-wide absence; the agent must report 'no evidence found in the inspected locations' rather than 'the capability does not exist.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: DeclaredArchitecture ... ImplementedArchitecture ... VerifiedBehavior
b_rows_sample.statement: E3 Inspect distinguishes evidence types by artifact kind: documentation establishes DeclaredArchitecture, source code establishes ImplementedArchitecture, tests establish VerifiedBehavior — these are different evidence types and must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The objective is not simply finding matching names. It is establishing semantic linkage.
b_rows_sample.statement: E4 Trace: given a claim Decision -> Implementation, the agent follows the chain Decision -> ADR/record -> change request -> PR -> commit -> artifact -> deployment, aiming at semantic linkage rather than textual name-matching; defines traceability-strength scale T0 (no link) < T1 (textual similarity) < T2 (explicit reference) < T3 (machine-readable identifier) < T4 (verified causal/implementation relationship), e.g. an ADR-042 identifier appearing in a commit is stronger evidence than shared wording.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Static / Unit / Integration / Architecture / Deployment / Runtime
b_rows_sample.statement: E5 Test: for a behavioral claim (e.g. 'authoritative knowledge cannot be created without provenance'), execute a concrete test (create(authoritative=true, provenance=null) expecting Reject) and classify it on a six-level test hierarchy (Static, Unit, Integration, Architecture, Deployment, Runtime) since the test type affects what the result actually proves.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Static code is not enough for operational claims.
b_rows_sample.statement: E6 Observe: operational claims (e.g. 'Nexus runs rootless') require inspecting actual runtime/deployment/logs/metrics/events, not merely a static configuration file such as a Podman config.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FACT | INFERENCE | TARGET | GAP
b_rows_sample.statement: E7 Classify: every finding receives one of four epistemic classifications — FACT (directly evidenced, e.g. a Containerfile using a specified base image, via E2/E3), INFERENCE (a reasoned interpretation that must not be presented as established fact without stronger evidence, e.g. 'this repo appears to implement the Evidence bounded context'), TARGET (intended future architecture unless implementation proves otherwise, e.g. 'KnowledgeOS should provide closed-loop governance'), GAP (Expected ≠ Observed, e.g. architecture requires provenance but authoritative records can currently be created without it).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM / FACTS / EVIDENCE / INFERENCE / VERIFICATION / GAP / TARGET / CONFIDENCE
b_rows_sample.statement: E8 Report: the final report must never collapse evidence into one narrative; it uses a fixed section format (Claim, Facts, Evidence, Inference, Verification, Gap, Target, Confidence) 'to prevent architectural contamination,' illustrated with a worked standard-agent-output example ending in STATUS: CONFORMANT / CONFIDENCE: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C0=Unknown, C1=Weak, C2=Moderate, C3=Strong, C4=Verified
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-level ordinal confidence scale (C0 Unknown .. C4 Verified) as superior to arbitrary percentages; argues LLMConfidence ≠ EvidenceConfidence because an LLM stating '95% confident' does not establish a quantitative probability, whereas evidence-derived confidence must derive from evidence quality; also distinguishes EvidenceStrength from Confidence (strong evidence can still leave interpretive ambiguity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: If evidence is insufficient, the agent MUST preserve UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: States an agent stopping rule / anti-hallucination rule: when evidence is insufficient the agent must preserve UNKNOWN rather than fill the gap from general knowledge; explicitly frames stopping with disclosed uncertainty (e.g. 'implementation is supported, enforcement is unverified') as a successful investigation, not a failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mode A — Architecture reconstruction ... Mode E — Knowledge reconstruction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five repository investigation modes with distinct evidence focus — A Architecture reconstruction (Structure+Dependencies), B Governance verification (Authority+Decision+Process), C Assurance verification (Rule+Test+Evidence), D Runtime verification (Deployment+Observation), E Knowledge reconstruction (Meaning+Provenance+Validity) — and requires the agent to select the mode before searching, and to follow a Broad->Narrow->Exact->Trace search strategy (e.g. 'provenance' -> 'source_id' -> 'createKnowledge' -> tests -> runtime).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the invariant be bypassed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against name-based conclusions (e.g. a class named ProvenanceService does not itself prove provenance is enforced — the agent must ask who calls it, when, what happens on failure, whether the result is persisted, and whether it can be bypassed); defines the enforcement test 'can the invariant be bypassed? If yes, Enforcement<Strong,' illustrated by Experiment 2 where a ProvenanceService exists but developers can insert DB records without provenance, yielding Declared=Yes, Enforced=No, verdict PARTIAL.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C1 ... provenance required ... direct persistence | C7 ... feedback path exists ... finding dead-end
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 120 C1-C7 constitution with a bypass-question and bypass-test matrix per invariant: C1 can authoritative knowledge bypass provenance via direct persistence; C2 can approval bypass authority via unauthorized promotion; C3 can inference be promoted to authority without validation; C4 can stale knowledge appear current via stale retrieval; C5 can verification results be fabricated/irreproducible via inconsistent rerun; C6 can governed actions occur without traceability via untracked action; C7 can findings disappear without governance closure via finding dead-end — presented as a practical assurance test suite.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. State the claim. ... 10. Never promote inference to authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a ten-item 'agent execution contract' every KnowledgeOS-aware engineering agent must follow: state the claim; identify evidence sources; inspect implementation; trace relationships; execute relevant tests where possible; inspect runtime where required; separate fact from inference; report uncertainty; identify gaps; never promote inference to authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameAuthority / SameEvidenceRules / SameConstitution / SameEpistemicDiscipline
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that Claude and Codex should share the Evidence Execution Protocol as a common agent-instruction layer: the important symmetry is not identical configuration but SameAuthority, SameEvidenceRules, SameConstitution, SameEpistemicDiscipline, while Claude and Codex harnesses remain operationally different — diagrammed as KnowledgeOS -> Evidence Protocol -> {Claude Harness, Codex Harness} -> Same Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is a pointer/behavior contract, not a duplicate knowledge repository.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a minimal KnowledgeOS-aware AGENTS.md operating contract (consult authoritative sources, verify current validity, preserve provenance, distinguish fact from inference, use deterministic checks where available, record material engineering actions against authorization, never treat local agent memory as authoritative) and states that .claude/ and .codex/ should likewise hold tools/hooks/workflow/session-behavior/verification-procedures/pointers-to-KnowledgeOS but must not become the enterprise architecture authority themselves — the goal is OperationalSymmetry without KnowledgeDuplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: # Evidence Execution Report ... Open questions: ...
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a standard 'Evidence Execution Report' template with fields Claim, Scope, Evidence inspected, Implementation, Tests executed, Runtime observations, FACT, INFERENCE, TARGET, GAP, Conformance, Confidence, Open questions, as the mandatory end-of-investigation deliverable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes judging an agent by EvidenceQuality rather than AnswerQuality: an articulate but unsupported answer should score poorly, a cautious evidence-backed answer highly; defines AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline), explicitly preferable to measuring only LLMAnswerSimilarity; further defines Completeness = VerifiedLinks/RequiredLinks for a claim needing n evidence links, notes critical missing links should carry higher weight (WeightedCompleteness preferable to plain Completeness), and gives Authority as an example of a critical link whose absence should not be masked by ten present technical links.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim ├── supportedBy → Evidence ... └── classifiedAs → Status
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes that an agent's own investigation becomes graph data (Claim -supportedBy-> Evidence, -verifiedBy-> Test, -observedAt-> Runtime, -interpretedAs-> Finding, -classifiedAs-> Status), so the process of understanding the architecture itself becomes part of KnowledgeOS knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model | 5 independent converging passes | Candidate
a_rows_sample.statement: The dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model is held as a Candidate architectural hypothesis, supported by 5 independent converging passes; movement requires an MM-1 ruling and D-8 reconciliation, decided by the ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This projection decides nothing and is authoritative for nothing
a_rows_sample.statement: The dashboard is explicitly non-authoritative and non-deciding: it exists only so humans can see, on one page, what architectural hypotheses are being tested and what evidence would count as a result; rows change only on evidence or an authority ruling, never on a schedule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal. ... EXTERNAL RESEARCH ≠ KNOWLEDGEOS ARCHITECTURE
a_rows_sample.statement: The document repeatedly and explicitly frames itself as an independent external-research evidence base for later comparison against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP architectures, and NOT itself a KnowledgeOS architecture proposal; the closing discipline statement instructs: do not design the kernel, do not choose technology, do not define bounded contexts, do not create ADRs, do not propose migration -- 'the output is an independent research evidence base for a later architecture decision.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries. Therefore strict bounded contexts may fragment knowledge unnecessarily. ... DDD is less clearly validated as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD concepts (ownership, invariants, policies, language) help model knowledge-system governance, but evidence is mixed on DDD as a universal organizing principle for knowledge representation, because knowledge often crosses organizational boundaries and strict bounded contexts may fragment it unnecessarily.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is no established academic architecture pattern known as a 'Knowledge Operating System.' ... KnowledgeOS is not entering an established category.
a_rows_sample.statement: Direct research into 'Knowledge Operating System' terminology finds only vendor marketing, AI-memory platforms, experimental open-source projects, and personal knowledge tools; there is no established academic architecture pattern by this name, and the term is currently emerging, inconsistent, and frequently marketing-driven -- therefore KnowledgeOS (this project) is not entering an established research category.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No mature research field appears to define a universally accepted: knowledge kernel, epistemic kernel, organizational memory kernel ... The term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Direct research finding: no mature research field defines a universally accepted 'knowledge kernel', 'epistemic kernel', or 'organizational memory kernel' -- the term exists mostly as metaphor, prototype vocabulary, or isolated conceptual work; this is recorded as a research gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Research on operating systems repeatedly emphasizes: stable primitives, minimal trusted core, separation of mechanism and policy, composability ... Knowledge systems lack: deterministic execution, strict process isolation, universal semantics ... OS analogies are useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Unix/Linux analogy is architecturally useful for stable primitives, a minimal trusted core, mechanism/policy separation, and composability, but knowledge systems lack the deterministic execution, strict process isolation, and universal semantics of operating systems -- OS analogies are 'useful heuristics, not architectural proofs.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Successful ecosystems often separate: core standards, extensibility mechanisms, commercial capabilities. Governance and interoperability matter more than licensing for architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Comparative research on open-source vs commercial architecture finds that successful ecosystems separate core standards, extensibility mechanisms, and commercial capabilities, and that governance and interoperability matter more than licensing model for architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Debate | Position A | Position B ... Knowledge structure Graph/Documents ... History Events/State+history ... No universal winner exists. Context determines suitability.
a_rows_sample.statement: The literature contains unresolved cross-research contradictions with no universal winner: Knowledge structure (Graph vs Documents), History (Events vs State+history), Semantics (Ontology-first vs Emergent), Governance (Strong approval vs Collaborative editing), Consistency (Deterministic vs Probabilistic), Memory (Centralized vs Federated), AI (AI-centric vs Human-centric); context determines suitability in each case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The literature remains weak regarding: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Six research gaps are recorded: organizational epistemic kernels, authority modeling as a distinct primitive, institutional memory architectures, long-horizon decision lineage, provenance-aware AI governance, and knowledge operating systems as a formal discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No conclusion can yet be drawn regarding: kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, AI integration. Those remain comparison questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document explicitly refuses to draw conclusions about kernel structure, domain model, bounded contexts, storage architecture, graph centrality, event sourcing, or AI integration for KnowledgeOS -- these are labelled comparison questions to be resolved only against reconstructed EKS/PKS/AIP evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Those are excellent research candidates, but we must now label them: EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE ↓ NOT YET ↓ KnowledgeOS kernel candidate
a_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a mandatory classification-layer discipline when consuming the external research's 'Smallest Trustworthy Core' list: every candidate must be explicitly labelled EXTERNAL RESEARCH CANDIDATE -> NOT YET -> KnowledgeOS kernel candidate, because the source research itself says these must still be compared with EKS/PKS/AIP.

a_rows_sample.anchor: So now we have three evidence layers ... CURRENT SYSTEMS / EXTERNAL RESEARCH / INTERNAL HYPOTHESES ... CROSS-SYSTEM COMPARISON ↓ DDD VALIDATION ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATES ↓ HUMAN ARCHITECTURE DECISION
a_rows_sample.statement: Commentary pass proposes a three-evidence-layer investigation model (Current Systems=EKS/PKS/AIP; External Research=KMS/AKM/PROV/epistemic systems/organizational memory/temporal systems; Internal Hypotheses=brainstorming corpus) feeding a pipeline of Cross-System Comparison -> DDD Validation -> Kernel Candidates -> Human Architecture Decision, and recommends stopping broad external-research collection in favour of the comparison phase.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?'
a_rows_sample.statement: The commentary pass reframes the driving research question from 'What should a KnowledgeOS kernel contain?' to 'Which of these externally validated principles are already embodied in EKS, PKS, or AIP, which are missing, which are duplicated, and which would actually require a new KnowledgeOS kernel boundary?' -- framed as the investigation that determines whether any kernel is a real extraction from the existing ecosystem rather than an invented new system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The term 'Knowledge Operating System' appears primarily in industry/marketing contexts ... a LinkedIn article (2026) describes a 'Knowledge Operating System' as treating organizational knowledge as governed infrastructure, compiling knowledge into a persistent wiki, versioned, auditable, access-controlled.
a_rows_sample.statement: Second-pass draft adds a dedicated 'Knowledge Operating System terminology' section (not present as a distinct section in pass 1): the term appears in a 2026 LinkedIn article describing a KOS as governed infrastructure compiled into a persistent, versioned, auditable, access-controlled wiki, but no peer-reviewed literature establishes 'Knowledge OS' as a canonical architecture pattern; related terms ('knowledge infrastructure', 'knowledge runtime', 'knowledge kernel') appear sporadically without established definitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They are not two independent architectural authorities. They overlap heavily: Research 1 + Research 2 ↓ External Research Corpus ↓ Research-supported hypotheses
a_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass instructs that the two research drafts must be treated as one combined external research corpus rather than two independent architectural authorities, since they overlap heavily and both ultimately conclude 'External research does not establish the KnowledgeOS kernel.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of semantic and mechanical primitives that must be universally trustworthy for an organizational knowledge system — and which of those primitives are actually demonstrated as cross-cutting concerns in EKS, PKS, and AIP? ... let EKS/PKS/AIP evidence eliminate candidates, not merely confirm the research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final commentary pass proposes the next precise research question (given the external evidence corpus, what is the smallest set of universally-trustworthy primitives, and which are demonstrated cross-cutting in EKS/PKS/AIP) plus a draft comparison matrix (Candidate x External evidence x EKS x PKS x AIP x Cross-cutting? x Kernel candidate?) for Identity, Provenance, Temporal validity, Authority, Evidence, Decision, Lineage, Lifecycle, Conflict, Assurance -- and states the crucial methodological principle that EKS/PKS/AIP evidence should be used to ELIMINATE candidates, not merely confirm the external research, 'to give a defensible KnowledgeOS kernel rather than a kernel designed from literature alone.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not interpret DeepSeek's report as: 'We discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel.' I would interpret it as: 'We discovered that EKS, PKS and AIP already contain a recurring family of epistemic and governance invariants that are stronger than their current architectural boundaries suggest.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit reframing/caution: DeepSeek's report should not be read as 'we discovered the KnowledgeOS kernel' but as 'EKS, PKS, and AIP already contain a recurring family of epistemic and governance invariants stronger than their current architectural boundaries suggest' -- a more valuable, more modest finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS invariant ↓ PKS equivalent ↓ AIP equivalent ↓ same semantic invariant? ↓ same lifecycle? ↓ same ownership? ↓ independent of domain? ↓ reusable abstraction? ↓ KERNEL CANDIDATE ↓ DDD validation ↓ KERNEL DECISION. The report explicitly says this progression has not yet been executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a next-step progression (an 'AMENDMENT-6 progression'): for each candidate, verify EKS invariant -> PKS equivalent -> AIP equivalent -> same semantic invariant? -> same lifecycle? -> same ownership? -> independent of domain? -> reusable abstraction? -> kernel candidate -> DDD validation -> kernel decision; explicitly states this progression has not yet been executed for any candidate, and recommends starting with C-1 (Authority-as-recorded-reference-to-a-human-act) as the strongest, since DeepSeek found essentially the same invariant explicitly represented across all three systems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vāṇī as Research Lens (Not Kernel Law) ... Valid Contributions: Expression ≠ Meaning ... Invalid Contributions: Vāṇī as kernel principle: Not supported (external authority) ... Sacred authority model: Domain-specific, not universal
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit classification of the Vāṇī/oral-tradition source material: valid contributions are Expression≠Meaning, knowledge-transmission-across-media, the weaving metaphor (relationships, supported by graph/invariant research), and the authority question (supported by governance/provenance research); invalid contributions are Vāṇī as a kernel principle (not supported -- an external authority claim), a sacred-authority model (domain-specific, not universal), and Expression as a kernel dimension (not supported).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the Constitution must explicitly state what KnowledgeOS refuses to become (not a repository · not an LLM · not a truth oracle · not a similarity engine · not an autonomous decision maker)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the Constitution to formalize a negative boundary — five explicit refusals of what KnowledgeOS is not — as a required chapter component alongside the eleven articles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Mathematical elegance ≠ Truth ... 4. Beautiful formula ≠ Authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Four dangerous misunderstandings explicitly rejected when importing Vedic Mathematics: mathematical elegance ≠ truth, speed ≠ quality, pattern similarity ≠ identity, beautiful formula ≠ authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not import: Revelation authority model, Religious truth hierarchy, Theology as kernel logic, Moral judgement engine. Because KnowledgeOS is domain-independent.
b_rows_sample.statement: States four explicit refusals against importing religious authority structures into KnowledgeOS, grounded in the domain-independence requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What must never be mistaken for knowledge? ... Source/Lens ↓ False identification ↓ Architectural danger ↓ KnowledgeOS boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: States that every mature epistemic system needs a negative definition (what knowledge is not) as much as a positive one, and proposes the negative-direction extraction method: source/lens → false identification → architectural danger → KnowledgeOS boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Data | Data lacks justified meaning ... LLM output | Generation is not knowledge | Database row | Storage is not epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Produces the consolidated fifteen-row 'negative character of KnowledgeOS' table (Data, Documents, Text, Search results, Similarity, Authority, Belief, Opinion, Probability, Prediction, Memory, Latest version, Consensus, LLM output, Database row), each with a stated reason it fails to be knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not a system that stores what is said, predicts what is likely, or preserves what is believed. It is a system that preserves the conditions under which claims can become justified, accountable, revisable knowledge. ... The strongest 'not' is: KnowledgeOS is NOT a truth generator.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ultimate negative definition and identifies the single deepest boundary — KnowledgeOS is NOT a truth generator, it prevents corruption of the path toward truth rather than manufacturing truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Positive: KnowledgeOS preserves the relationship between the Knower, the Known, the Evidence, and the evolution of understanding. Negative: KnowledgeOS prevents representations, opinions, predictions, authorities, and transformations from being mistaken for knowledge itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the two-part (positive+negative) character formulation as together forming the real boundary of the system — the first draft of an explicit negative-face character clause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The negative face was not absent from the architecture — Constitution Ch IV ... and UM-44/§AQ ... already carried it ... What was genuinely missing was the character-level negative complement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Precisely locates what the negative-epistemology synthesis actually adds: the constitutional/boundary-level negative face already existed (Ch IV, UM-44/§AQ); the missing piece was a character-level negative clause, brought here for the first time to the same depth as the positive character.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS prevents representations, opinions, predictions, authorities, and transformations from being mistaken for knowledge itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the first explicit negative-face character candidate, held PROPOSED until formal ratification; head 43 stands.

b_rows_sample.anchor: New namings: Consensus ≠ correctness and Prediction ≠ knowledge ... Latest version ≠ knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds new boundary-vocabulary namings (Consensus≠correctness, Prediction≠knowledge, Latest-version≠knowledge) to the consolidated not-list, each resolved as vocabulary rather than new content, routing to the Verification Gate/BD-4/Transformation articles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. KnowledgeOS is NOT trying to achieve human enlightenment ... 5. KnowledgeOS is NOT replacing humans
b_rows_sample.statement: States five explicit refusals of the Moksha lens's false mappings: not human enlightenment, not a consciousness engine, not a truth oracle, not removal of uncertainty, not human replacement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is NOT: A wisdom generator ... An autonomous philosopher ... A replacement for human judgement
b_rows_sample.statement: States three negative-boundary refusals specific to the wisdom layer: not a wisdom generator (only creates conditions for wisdom to emerge), not an autonomous philosopher (preserves accountable reasoning), not a replacement for human judgement (humans remain part of Knower/Context/Value/Purpose/Decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ❌ Truth Oracle ... ❌ Self-certified authority ... ❌ Self-modifying consciousness — the system reflects, human/governance validates, change occurs through a controlled process
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms three refusals from the Gödel angle: never a Truth Oracle, never self-certified authority, never a self-modifying consciousness — each a negative-face confirmation, not a new boundary.
