a_rows_sample.anchor: This is an EXPERIMENT. Do NOT modify the canonical theory merely to make the simulation pass. Do NOT silently repair definitions. Do NOT introduce undocumented assumptions. Do NOT treat a successful simulation as proof of the theory. Do NOT treat a failed simulation as proof that the theory is false.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the protocol's foundational experimental discipline: the theory must never be silently repaired or modified merely to make the simulation pass, no undocumented assumptions may be introduced, and neither a successful nor a failed simulation may be treated as proof or disproof of the theory -- the purpose is only to determine whether the theory is internally executable, semantically coherent, well-typed, and behaviorally stable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality, Observation, Information, Evidence, Interpretation, Hypothesis, Hypothesis Space, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Model, Determination, Knowledge Attribution, Epistemic State, Knowledge State K_t, Inquiry Q, Ideal State I_t, Requirements, Gap, Zero, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, History, Identity, Revision, Supersession. ... test whether these are genuinely distinct conceptual roles or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the primary research question: whether twenty-six named conceptual roles spanning the entire epistemic lifecycle can coexist operationally in one executable simulation without collapsing, or whether some are accidentally redundant, circular, or impossible to operationalize.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = Gamma(E_t, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) where Gamma determines which parts of the epistemic state qualify as Knowledge State content ... Knowledge remains factive: Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t). Do NOT operationally assume that the simulation can magically observe objective truth. If truth is externally supplied by the simulation world, explicitly label that as world-state information and keep it separate from the agent's epistemic state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the core theory-under-test's Knowledge Attribution mechanism K_t=Gamma(E_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) with mandatory factivity Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t), explicitly forbidding the simulation from assuming it can observe objective truth directly -- any world-supplied ground truth must be labelled as world-state information kept separate from the agent's own epistemic state (an oracle-vs-agent-knowledge separation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT make Bayesian likelihood ratios a universal KnowledgeOS law. Also test non-Bayesian / qualitative evidence assessment. ... Test whether changing epistemic standards can change assessment or determination while the underlying evidence remains identical. ... A model that fits simulated observations must not automatically be classified as true.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that evidence assessment be tested with BOTH a Bayesian likelihood-ratio realization AND non-Bayesian/qualitative assessment regimes (Bayesian ratios must never become a universal KnowledgeOS law); requires an explicit test that varying epistemic standards alone (holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed) can change assessment or determination; and requires model-fit to be tested separately from causal/epistemic validity so that a well-fitting model is never automatically classified as true.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality != Observation, Observation != Evidence, ... Epistemic State != Knowledge State, Knowledge State != Ideal State, Gap != Zero, Gap != Innovation, Probability != Truth, Credence != Truth, Information Quantity != Evidence Weight, Evidence Weight != Knowledge Gain, Model Fit != Model Validity, History != Current State, Identity != State Equality, Completeness != Sufficiency, Rejection != Acceptance, ... Semantic Equivalence != Representation Equality, Mathematical Regime != Knowledge Ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates a mandatory list of roughly twenty required state separations the simulator must never accidentally collapse (Reality/Observation/Evidence/Interpretation/Hypothesis/Determination/Knowledge/Decision/Authorization/Action chain; Epistemic State/Knowledge State/Ideal State; Gap/Zero/Innovation; Probability/Credence/Truth; Information Quantity/Evidence Weight/Knowledge Gain; Model Fit/Model Validity; History/Current State; Identity/State Equality; Completeness/Sufficiency; Rejection/Acceptance; Unknown/Unobserved/Unobservable/Underdetermined; Semantic Equivalence/Representation Equality; Mathematical Regime/Knowledge Ontology), with any collapse to be reported as a failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO A -- SIMPLE DETERMINATION ... SCENARIO B -- INCOMPLETE EVIDENCE ... Determination = empty or unresolved ... The system must NOT invent a value. This is an anti-fabrication test. ... SCENARIO C -- MULTIPLE COMPETING HYPOTHESES ... Test explicitly: Reject(H1) != Accept(H2). ... SCENARIO D -- DIFFERENT EPISTEMIC STANDARDS ... SCENARIO E -- DIFFERENT INQUIRIES
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten required scenario families (A-J): A simple determination (verifying knowledge is not merely copied from observation); B incomplete evidence (anti-fabrication test: the system must not invent a value when Determination is empty); C multiple competing hypotheses (testing Reject(H1)!=Accept(H2)); D different epistemic standards holding reality/observation/evidence/inquiry fixed while varying only S_t^epi; E different inquiries over the identical K_t testing inquiry-relative adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO F -- CONFLICTING EVIDENCE ... Do NOT automatically average them. ... The system can preserve unresolved conflict. SCENARIO G -- DEPENDENT EVIDENCE ... represent dependence, avoid double counting, or explicitly state that independence is an assumption. SCENARIO H -- MODEL MISMATCH ... Fit alone does not produce Knowledge. SCENARIO I -- RETROSPECTIVE REVISION ... Do NOT rewrite history as if K_1 never existed. SCENARIO J -- UNOBSERVABLE PROPERTY ... Do NOT classify this as: observed false, probability zero, rejected hypothesis, evidence absence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies scenario families F-J: F conflicting evidence (system must preserve unresolved conflict rather than automatically averaging); G dependent evidence (must represent dependence, avoid double-counting, or explicitly declare independence as an assumption); H model mismatch (a better-fitting but causally wrong model M1 versus a causally correct M2 -- fit alone must not produce Knowledge); I retrospective revision (K_2 != K_1, historical K_1 must remain traceable, never rewritten); J unobservable property (must be classified as Unknown/Unobservable, never as observed-false, probability-zero, rejected-hypothesis, or evidence-absence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED, UNINTERPRETED, UNDERDETERMINED, UNOBSERVABLE. Create test cases where each one occurs independently. ... Verify that the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a four-way Unknown taxonomy test with independently constructed test cases for each of Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable, checking Observation/Interpretation/Evidence/Determination/Knowledge/Gap/Zero status for each, explicitly verifying the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At every transition record: input state, output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information was added, whether uncertainty changed, whether knowledge attribution changed, whether requirements changed, whether the transition was reversible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace (Reality->Observation->Information->Evidence->Interpretation->HypothesisSpace->EvidenceAssessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t->Inquiry->IdealState->RequirementEvaluation->Gap->Zero->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action->newObservation->K_{t+1}) with eleven recorded facts at every single transition (input/output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information/uncertainty/attribution/requirements changed, reversibility).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If X -> Y -> Z and no new information enters between Y and Z, then Z must not magically contain semantic information unavailable in Y, except where explicitly introduced by: model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, standards. If new information appears, identify its source. Any unexplained semantic information creation is a critical failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates an Information Conservation test operationalizing the data-processing-inequality principle: no unexplained semantic information may appear between two steps with no new input, unless explicitly attributable to model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, or standards -- any unexplained semantic-information creation is a critical failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: high probability != knowledge, strong evidence != knowledge, coherent belief != knowledge, model fit != knowledge, determination != knowledge. ... If the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify the claim as Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Knowledge Attribution test constructing six epistemic-state cases (true/false/uncertain/rejected/highly-probable/justified-but-not-truth-verified hypotheses) and checking five non-collapse requirements (high probability, strong evidence, coherent belief, model fit, and determination all != knowledge); if the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify a claim as Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation A: explicit Interpret + Represent. Implementation B: single combined semantic transformation. Implementation C: different internal data structure. ... The comparison MUST NOT be based only on operator names. ... If semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior, report the circularity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Semantic Equivalence test comparing three deliberately different implementations of the same conceptual operation (split Interpret+Represent, a single combined transformation, and a different internal data structure) over nine behavioral dimensions (inquiries, context, evidence, determinations, gaps, history, transitions, knowledge attribution, invariant preservation), explicitly never based on operator names alone, and mandates reporting circularity if semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is NOT the previous 13-operator counting experiment. Do NOT begin with: "How many operators are there?" Instead ask: "What semantic capabilities are required?" ... K_min = argmin Complexity(R) subject to: semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, fixed semantic carrier, fixed observable behavior contract. If the feasible set changes between representations, cardinality comparisons are invalid. Report this explicitly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reframes the Kernel Minimality test away from the prior 13-operator counting approach: begin with 'what semantic capabilities are required' (Capability = externally distinguishable epistemic transformation/responsibility), construct the required capability set C and a candidate representation R, and test capability-set equivalence between differently-operator-counted implementations BEFORE any minimization; formalizes K_min=argmin Complexity(R) subject to six simultaneous constraints, mandating an explicit report that cardinality comparisons are invalid whenever the feasible set changes between representations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Investigate whether: Zero = no unmet requirement can be maintained without turning Zero into a semantic notion of absolute certainty. ... test all combinations: Gap exists, Gap empty, Evidence incomplete, Evidence conflicting, Evidence unavailable, Requirement irrelevant, Requirement satisfied by negative determination, Requirement satisfied by "cannot determine".
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Zero test evaluating Delta_t and Zero(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) across eight named combinations (gap exists/empty, evidence incomplete/conflicting/unavailable, requirement irrelevant, requirement satisfied by negative determination, requirement satisfied by 'cannot determine'), investigating whether Zero can be maintained as no-unmet-requirement without sliding into a semantic notion of absolute certainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create cases where: determination is unique but multiple actions are possible. Expected: Determination does not automatically imply one Decision. ... decision exists but authorization is absent. Expected: Decision != Authorization. ... authorization exists but action does not occur. Expected: Authorization != Action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Decision Boundary test with three constructed cases proving Determination does not automatically imply one Decision, Decision != Authorization (decision without authorization), and Authorization != Action (authorization without resulting action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X causes Y but an observed confounder Z creates a strong association. Also create: X and Y correlated but X does not cause Y. ... The result must distinguish: Association, Prediction, Explanation, Causal Claim. A fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Causal/Statistical test with two constructed confounding scenarios (X causes Y with a confounding Z creating spurious association; X and Y correlated with no causal link), requiring the system to distinguish Association, Prediction, Explanation, and Causal Claim as four separate categories -- a fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. highly probable but false claim 2. true claim with weak evidence 3. duplicated evidence 4. correlated evidence 5. misleading source ... 18. conclusion generated without supporting evidence. The simulator must prefer: "cannot determine" over fabricated certainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates eighteen named adversarial test cases explicitly designed to fool the simulator (highly-probable-but-false claim, true-claim-with-weak-evidence, duplicated/correlated evidence, misleading source, wrong-model-with-excellent-fit, correct-model-with-sparse-evidence, rejected-hypothesis-later-reinstated, ambiguous interpretation, representation change, changing inquiry/standard, unavailable observation, historical-vs-current state, conflicting/irrelevant evidence, false inference from correlation, unsupported conclusion), with the overriding requirement that the simulator prefer 'cannot determine' over fabricated certainty in every case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Evidence != Knowledge ... P8: Evidence dependence prevents unjustified double counting ... P11: Knowledge attribution respects factivity ... P19: Changing K_t does not imply changing identity ... P20: Zero is inquiry-relative. ... For each property define: Property ID, Formal statement, Generator assumptions, Test procedure, Observed result, Counterexamples.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates property-based testing with a required protocol per property (ID, formal statement, generator assumptions, test procedure, observed result, counterexamples), specifying twenty named minimum properties P1-P20 spanning Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Rejection!=Acceptance, Gap!=Zero, inquiry-relative adequacy, historical-vs-current-state distinguishability, representation-vs-semantic equality, dependence-aware evidence, model-fit-vs-causal-validity, no-unsupported-information-creation, factivity-respecting attribution, standards-dependent assessment, Unobservable!=Underdetermined, Completeness!=Sufficiency, the Decision/Determination/Authorization/Action chain, CurrentState!=History, identity-preservation-under-state-change, and inquiry-relative Zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use at least 10,000 trials per major property family ... But DO NOT interpret the result as a population estimate about the real world. Monte Carlo uncertainty describes the simulator/generator. ... Always audit vacuity. If: guard_active = 0 then: 100% pass means nothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates Monte Carlo requirements (>=10,000 trials per major property family where computationally reasonable) explicitly forbidding interpretation as a real-world population estimate (Monte Carlo uncertainty describes only the simulator/generator), and mandates an always-run vacuity audit (guard_active=0 makes a 100% pass rate meaningless) -- directly carrying forward the vacuity-audit discipline discovered in the earlier kernel-reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every successful property identify exactly where the tested capability came from. Detect hidden capabilities embedded in: world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function. Particularly inspect: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a No-Smuggling Audit for every successful property, tracing exactly where the tested capability actually came from and checking nine possible hidden-capability locations (world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function), with particular scrutiny of nine named operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate) -- directly carrying forward the semantic-smuggling discipline from the kernel-reduction experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every corroboration-dependent conclusion in this programme rests on a component of a concept v1.2 declares OPEN. ... Dropping the source component collapses corroboration and flips every downstream result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Details result 5 (E4): dropping the observation model's source component collapses corroboration and flips determination/attribution/Zero, showing corroboration-dependent conclusions rest on a component the theory itself calls OPEN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The v1.2 run reuses the entire v1.1 pipeline unchanged, and replaces only the evaluation layer ... any difference between the v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory, not to the simulator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes the controlled-experiment design: the v1.1 pipeline (world, state, transitions) is reused byte-identical, so any difference between v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory change, not the simulator.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E1 | Do the three Zero readings ever disagree? | Yes -- on the fully determined case. ... E5 | What kind of thing is Zero, of the seven v1.2 candidates? | 2 refuted, 1 partial, 4 surviving
b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates the five formal experiments (E1 Zero-reading disagreement, E2 equality substitutability, E3 CE-1/CE-3 persistence, E4 OPEN-observation dependence, E5 which of seven Zero readings survive) with their one-line results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The weakening was productive. v1.2 did not repair a single v1.1 failure -- but it made two of them better diagnosed, exposed one defect v1.1's phrasing had hidden (Zero's ambiguity), and gave the programme a vocabulary in which "we do not know" is a first-class result rather than a hedge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers the comparison verdict: v1.2 repaired no v1.1 failure but improved diagnosis of two, exposed a hidden defect (Zero's ambiguity) v1.1's phrasing had concealed, and made 'unknown' a first-class result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NOT TESTED -- and under v1.2, not testable. ... A kernel cannot be selected while its operation semantics are open, and E1 shows even the closure predicate itself is ambiguous. This is v1.2 behaving correctly, not a shortfall of the experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers a stronger kernel-status verdict than v1.1: not merely untested but not-yet-testable under v1.2's own declared openness of operation semantics and closure predicate.

Fit alone does not produce Knowledge. SCENARIO I -- RETROSPECTIVE REVISION ... Do NOT rewrite history as if K_1 never existed. SCENARIO J -- UNOBSERVABLE PROPERTY ... Do NOT classify this as: observed false, probability zero, rejected hypothesis, evidence absence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies scenario families F-J: F conflicting evidence (system must preserve unresolved conflict rather than automatically averaging); G dependent evidence (must represent dependence, avoid double-counting, or explicitly declare independence as an assumption); H model mismatch (a better-fitting but causally wrong model M1 versus a causally correct M2 -- fit alone must not produce Knowledge); I retrospective revision (K_2 != K_1, historical K_1 must remain traceable, never rewritten); J unobservable property (must be classified as Unknown/Unobservable, never as observed-false, probability-zero, rejected-hypothesis, or evidence-absence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UNOBSERVED, UNINTERPRETED, UNDERDETERMINED, UNOBSERVABLE. Create test cases where each one occurs independently. ... Verify that the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a four-way Unknown taxonomy test with independently constructed test cases for each of Unobserved/Uninterpreted/Underdetermined/Unobservable, checking Observation/Interpretation/Evidence/Determination/Knowledge/Gap/Zero status for each, explicitly verifying the four cases do not collapse into one generic UNKNOWN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At every transition record: input state, output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information was added, whether uncertainty changed, whether knowledge attribution changed, whether requirements changed, whether the transition was reversible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a full 21-step epistemic lifecycle trace (Reality->Observation->Information->Evidence->Interpretation->HypothesisSpace->EvidenceAssessment->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution->K_t->Inquiry->IdealState->RequirementEvaluation->Gap->Zero->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action->newObservation->K_{t+1}) with eleven recorded facts at every single transition (input/output state, transformation, provenance, assumptions, responsible conceptual role, whether semantic information/uncertainty/attribution/requirements changed, reversibility).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If X -> Y -> Z and no new information enters between Y and Z, then Z must not magically contain semantic information unavailable in Y, except where explicitly introduced by: model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, standards. If new information appears, identify its source. Any unexplained semantic information creation is a critical failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates an Information Conservation test operationalizing the data-processing-inequality principle: no unexplained semantic information may appear between two steps with no new input, unless explicitly attributable to model assumptions, external information, inference rules, prior knowledge, or standards -- any unexplained semantic-information creation is a critical failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: high probability != knowledge, strong evidence != knowledge, coherent belief != knowledge, model fit != knowledge, determination != knowledge. ... If the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify the claim as Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Knowledge Attribution test constructing six epistemic-state cases (true/false/uncertain/rejected/highly-probable/justified-but-not-truth-verified hypotheses) and checking five non-collapse requirements (high probability, strong evidence, coherent belief, model fit, and determination all != knowledge); if the simulator cannot establish Truth independently, it must not silently classify a claim as Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation A: explicit Interpret + Represent. Implementation B: single combined semantic transformation. Implementation C: different internal data structure. ... The comparison MUST NOT be based only on operator names. ... If semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior, report the circularity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Semantic Equivalence test comparing three deliberately different implementations of the same conceptual operation (split Interpret+Represent, a single combined transformation, and a different internal data structure) over nine behavioral dimensions (inquiries, context, evidence, determinations, gaps, history, transitions, knowledge attribution, invariant preservation), explicitly never based on operator names alone, and mandates reporting circularity if semantic equivalence cannot be defined independently of behavior.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is NOT the previous 13-operator counting experiment. Do NOT begin with: "How many operators are there?" Instead ask: "What semantic capabilities are required?" ... K_min = argmin Complexity(R) subject to: semantic adequacy, transition completeness, invariant preservation, capability completeness, fixed semantic carrier, fixed observable behavior contract. If the feasible set changes between representations, cardinality comparisons are invalid. Report this explicitly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reframes the Kernel Minimality test away from the prior 13-operator counting approach: begin with 'what semantic capabilities are required' (Capability = externally distinguishable epistemic transformation/responsibility), construct the required capability set C and a candidate representation R, and test capability-set equivalence between differently-operator-counted implementations BEFORE any minimization; formalizes K_min=argmin Complexity(R) subject to six simultaneous constraints, mandating an explicit report that cardinality comparisons are invalid whenever the feasible set changes between representations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Investigate whether: Zero = no unmet requirement can be maintained without turning Zero into a semantic notion of absolute certainty. ... test all combinations: Gap exists, Gap empty, Evidence incomplete, Evidence conflicting, Evidence unavailable, Requirement irrelevant, Requirement satisfied by negative determination, Requirement satisfied by "cannot determine".
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Zero test evaluating Delta_t and Zero(K_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t) across eight named combinations (gap exists/empty, evidence incomplete/conflicting/unavailable, requirement irrelevant, requirement satisfied by negative determination, requirement satisfied by 'cannot determine'), investigating whether Zero can be maintained as no-unmet-requirement without sliding into a semantic notion of absolute certainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create cases where: determination is unique but multiple actions are possible. Expected: Determination does not automatically imply one Decision. ... decision exists but authorization is absent. Expected: Decision != Authorization. ... authorization exists but action does not occur. Expected: Authorization != Action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Decision Boundary test with three constructed cases proving Determination does not automatically imply one Decision, Decision != Authorization (decision without authorization), and Authorization != Action (authorization without resulting action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X causes Y but an observed confounder Z creates a strong association. Also create: X and Y correlated but X does not cause Y. ... The result must distinguish: Association, Prediction, Explanation, Causal Claim. A fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a Causal/Statistical test with two constructed confounding scenarios (X causes Y with a confounding Z creating spurious association; X and Y correlated with no causal link), requiring the system to distinguish Association, Prediction, Explanation, and Causal Claim as four separate categories -- a fitted model is insufficient for causal determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. highly probable but false claim 2. true claim with weak evidence 3. duplicated evidence 4. correlated evidence 5. misleading source ... 18. conclusion generated without supporting evidence. The simulator must prefer: "cannot determine" over fabricated certainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates eighteen named adversarial test cases explicitly designed to fool the simulator (highly-probable-but-false claim, true-claim-with-weak-evidence, duplicated/correlated evidence, misleading source, wrong-model-with-excellent-fit, correct-model-with-sparse-evidence, rejected-hypothesis-later-reinstated, ambiguous interpretation, representation change, changing inquiry/standard, unavailable observation, historical-vs-current state, conflicting/irrelevant evidence, false inference from correlation, unsupported conclusion), with the overriding requirement that the simulator prefer 'cannot determine' over fabricated certainty in every case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1: Evidence != Knowledge ... P8: Evidence dependence prevents unjustified double counting ... P11: Knowledge attribution respects factivity ... P19: Changing K_t does not imply changing identity ... P20: Zero is inquiry-relative. ... For each property define: Property ID, Formal statement, Generator assumptions, Test procedure, Observed result, Counterexamples.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates property-based testing with a required protocol per property (ID, formal statement, generator assumptions, test procedure, observed result, counterexamples), specifying twenty named minimum properties P1-P20 spanning Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Knowledge, Rejection!=Acceptance, Gap!=Zero, inquiry-relative adequacy, historical-vs-current-state distinguishability, representation-vs-semantic equality, dependence-aware evidence, model-fit-vs-causal-validity, no-unsupported-information-creation, factivity-respecting attribution, standards-dependent assessment, Unobservable!=Underdetermined, Completeness!=Sufficiency, the Decision/Determination/Authorization/Action chain, CurrentState!=History, identity-preservation-under-state-change, and inquiry-relative Zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use at least 10,000 trials per major property family ... But DO NOT interpret the result as a population estimate about the real world. Monte Carlo uncertainty describes the simulator/generator. ... Always audit vacuity. If: guard_active = 0 then: 100% pass means nothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates Monte Carlo requirements (>=10,000 trials per major property family where computationally reasonable) explicitly forbidding interpretation as a real-world population estimate (Monte Carlo uncertainty describes only the simulator/generator), and mandates an always-run vacuity audit (guard_active=0 makes a 100% pass rate meaningless) -- directly carrying forward the vacuity-audit discipline discovered in the earlier kernel-reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every successful property identify exactly where the tested capability came from. Detect hidden capabilities embedded in: world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function. Particularly inspect: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a No-Smuggling Audit for every successful property, tracing exactly where the tested capability actually came from and checking nine possible hidden-capability locations (world generator, data structure, serializer, simulator helper, test oracle, random generator, state constructor, hard-coded labels, evaluation function), with particular scrutiny of nine named operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Determine, Select, Revise, Validate) -- directly carrying forward the semantic-smuggling discipline from the kernel-reduction experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-01: No agent component may become the system of record for authoritative organizational knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-01, protecting the KnowledgeOS boundary against agent components becoming the authoritative system of record.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-02: Authoritative knowledge must have explicit provenance and authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-02, requiring explicit provenance and authority for authoritative knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-03: External system models must not leak directly into KnowledgeOS domain semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-03, requiring adapters/translation so external system models do not leak into KnowledgeOS domain semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-04: Assurance detects conformance; governance determines disposition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-04, preventing technical verification from becoming organizational authority by separating detection (Assurance) from disposition (Governance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-05: Agent recommendations must remain distinguishable from authoritative decisions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-05, requiring agent recommendations to remain distinguishable from authoritative decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-06: Material agent actions require traceable authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-06, requiring traceable authorization for material agent actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-07: Every material change must produce sufficient evidence for post-action verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-07, creating the closure mechanism by requiring sufficient evidence for post-action verification of every material change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-08: Constitutional rules must be independently testable where technically feasible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-08, connecting architecture governance to deterministic assurance by requiring constitutional rules to be independently testable where feasible.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-09: Historical authoritative states must remain reconstructable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-09, requiring historical authoritative states to remain reconstructable since current knowledge alone is insufficient for auditability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-10: Unknown must remain a valid epistemic outcome.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture Fitness Rule AFR-10, requiring the system never manufacture certainty merely because an agent is expected to provide an answer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Let the Claude .claude/memory/ directory become the primary source of architectural knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked context-map/AFR-01 test: a proposal to make Claude's .claude/memory/ the primary architectural-knowledge source FAILs AFR-01 since AgentLocalMemory ≠ AuthoritativeKnowledge; correct architecture has authoritative knowledge flowing KnowledgeOS -> Claude memory/cache, not the reverse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AGENTS.md → KnowledgeOS. Not AGENTS.md = KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked context-map tests for Codex (AGENTS.md is acceptable only as a pointer/operating contract, with authoritative knowledge remaining in KnowledgeOS: AGENTS.md -> KnowledgeOS, never AGENTS.md = KnowledgeOS) and Claude (.claude/ owns agent behavior/hooks/workflow/configuration/pointers while KnowledgeOS owns authoritative engineering knowledge/governance/evidence/decisions — giving the desired symmetry) and Nexus (a Nexus config statement like 'Repository X is authoritative' is operational evidence, NexusConfig->Observation/Evidence, not automatically the enterprise architecture decision, which instead comes from GovernanceDecision->ExpectedArchitecture, compared by the assurance layer).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Principle → Fitness Rule → Automated Check → Evidence → Verdict
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 129 (KnowledgeOS Architecture Fitness Model): rather than merely documenting principles like 'agents must not become authoritative,' defines an executable pipeline Architecture Principle -> Fitness Rule -> Automated Check -> Evidence -> Verdict able to inspect repository structure, dependencies, configuration, agent harnesses, KnowledgeOS APIs, governance records, evidence, and CI pipelines — the bridge from DDD architecture to deterministic architectural assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-11: Agent components may consume authoritative knowledge through approved interfaces, but must not establish independent authoritative stores.
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-11 operationalizes the Claude/Codex symmetry principle as a structural/dependency-graph check (forbidden edge Agent->AuthorityStore, E_forbidden ∩ E = ∅); worked agent-memory test — a .claude/memory/ file independently asserting 'ADR-42 is authoritative' FAILs, while one reading 'see KnowledgeOS decision ADR-42' PASSes (a pointer, not an independent authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-12: AGENTS.md may define agent behavior/workflow/pointers/constraints but must not silently become the enterprise architecture system of record.
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-12 restricts AGENTS.md's role, paralleling AFR-11 for the Codex harness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-13: "Approved" must have one governed meaning within the relevant bounded context.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces SemanticFitness beyond structural rules — code can compile perfectly while semantic integrity breaks (e.g. two contexts using 'Approved' to mean ApprovedDecision vs ApprovedDeployment, not the same concept), formalized as AFR-13, a Ubiquitous Language rule requiring one governed meaning per bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ContextA → Contract → ContextB.
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-14: only the owning context may perform invariant-sensitive state transitions on its own aggregates (a classic DDD fitness rule) — a bounded context must not directly manipulate another's aggregates (e.g. Engineering must not directly set governance.decision.status=approved; instead Engineering->GovernanceContract, with Governance owning the transition), enforced via ContextA->Contract->ContextB rather than direct aggregate mutation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-15: Every authoritative decision must reference valid authority. ... ValidAuthority(a,t).
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-15 (forall d in Decisions: Authoritative(d) => ValidAuthority(d)) accounts for temporal authority validity ValidAuthority(a,t); worked Experiment 1 — a delegation valid 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 with a decision dated 2026-07-15 yields ValidAuthority=False, expected FAIL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-16: Every active exception must have authority, scope, and expiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-16 requires Exception->Authority, Exception->Scope, Exception->Validity; warns against a 'temporary exception' record with no expiry (Expiry=null yields FAIL), preventing temporary architecture from becoming permanent through neglect.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AFR-17: Material authoritative knowledge must have traceable supporting evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: AFR-17 requires traceable supporting evidence for evidence-requiring knowledge classes (not necessarily every piece of text); evidence should carry enough metadata to establish Who/What/When/FromWhere, potentially Hash and Version; runtime assertions specifically need ObservedAt, otherwise a statement like 'Service X runs version 5' has no temporal meaning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does Codex consume the same knowledge authority? If not: KnowledgeAuthorityFragmentation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies the Claude harness as AgentIntegration (instructions/settings/hooks/commands/memory/workflow, explicitly not enterprise knowledge authority) and poses the Codex symmetry question — if Codex consumes the same knowledge authority, semantic symmetry is achieved; if not, KnowledgeAuthorityFragmentation results; diagrams the pointer-layer architecture (Authoritative Knowledge -> {Claude Adapter->.claude/->Agent, Codex Adapter->.codex/->Agent}).

b_rows_sample.anchor: PLP-01: Agent-specific artifacts may point to authoritative engineering knowledge but must not silently redefine it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies AGENTS.md as an OperatingContract boundary artifact (how the agent should behave, how to discover KnowledgeOS, what tools may be used, what verification is required) that must not become KnowledgeAuthority, formalizing the Pointer-Layer Principle PLP-01, applying to Claude, Codex, and future agents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent observation → Local memory → Candidate claim → Evidence → Verification → Governed knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends PLP-01 to .claude/memory/ (desired status ContextualMemory, potentially CandidateKnowledge, but not automatically AuthoritativeKnowledge), giving the full memory-promotion pipeline, and requiring investigation of whether the existing session-logging/observation/knowledge-artifact/verification/governance mechanisms are explicitly connected or merely adjacent.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-pointer-layer-principle' POSSIBLY relates to 'kos-architecture-fitness-rules' (batch B0025). Note: Step 134's Pointer-Layer Principle PLP-01 (agent-specific artifacts, e.g. AGENTS.md/.claude/.codex/memory, may point to authoritative knowledge but must not silently redefine it) and the diagrammed pointer-layer architecture, operationalizing the same concern as AFR-11/AFR-12 with a distinct named principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS =/= LLM =/= Database =/= Search Engine =/= Truth Oracle
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 1 (Character Definition) requirements: answer 'What is KnowledgeOS?' including purpose, boundary, what it protects, what it enables; must explicitly distinguish KnowledgeOS from LLM, Database, Search Engine, and Truth Oracle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The answer map — every commissioned question → its existing answer
b_rows_sample.statement: A table maps eleven commissioned questions (mission, vision, domains, bounded contexts, core/supporting/generic, context map, lifecycle, knowledge flow, capability model, runtime boundary, PKS boundary, product boundary) to where each is already answered in the frozen corpus, with a grade (Confirmed/Candidate/Hypothesis/Open Question), whether it was blind-validated, and the gate door it routes to.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-10 | Mission —enacted by→ machinery | HIGH
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-10: Mission is enacted by machinery. External support: Argyris & Schön theory-in-use (organizations act on unwritten theory) is the relation itself, CANONICAL. No challenge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mission ENACTED, unratified ... Argyris & Schön: espoused theory vs THEORY-IN-USE
b_rows_sample.statement: The 'mission enacted, unratified' finding is a named organizational-theory phenomenon: Argyris & Schön's espoused-theory-vs-theory-in-use distinction — organizations act on theories they have not written, and the written and enacted routinely diverge. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "Mission is ENACTED" replaces "mission is implicit"
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Mission is ENACTED' replaces 'mission is implicit' as a stronger and more accurate statement: the platform is not describing its mission, it is already behaving according to it. The reviewer's hierarchy is adopted structurally: documents become the lowest layer of the model, never its centre.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
b_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

b_rows_sample.anchor: PURPOSE | no decision has been changed by consulting the mission (enacted, UNRATIFIED — D-5 pending)
b_rows_sample.statement: PURPOSE also supports no observable decision: no decision has changed by consulting the mission, and its use in the ontology pass was a test, not a decision. Judgment suspended: an unratified purpose cannot yet support decisions; D-5 decides whether it starts to.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "TWO MISSIONS" IS WITHDRAWN — 2026-08-02 ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION ... THE MISSION IS IMPLICIT BUT EVIDENCED, NOT VACANT
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's own 'two missions' framing (elaborated in Part 1 below) is withdrawn: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission when it is a constraint/cost-control (it ships with a per-iteration metric and over-evolution trigger, which a mission does not have — and the document itself calls AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after naming it a mission, a direct self-contradiction). The replacing finding (corrected further at REV 2, recorded in KnowledgeOS_Vision_Mission_Clarification.md): the mission is implicit but evidenced, not vacant — evidenced by eight artifacts, none PublicDigit-specific (ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest question, ES-006.1's ladder, the Reference Architecture's independence clause, the capability-agnostic pattern, the reserved registry/ namespace, the pre-positioned Platform-equiv-Adoption split, ES-005.4). 'Vacant' was a third instance of one error: artifact absence != concept absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THERE ARE TWO MISSION STATEMENTS IN CANON, AND ONLY ONE IS ADOPTED ... M-A ADOPTED · M-B PROPOSED · UNAPPROVED
b_rows_sample.statement: Two mission statements found in canon: M-A (AIP-14/ADR-AIP-02/R-23), 'the platform exists solely to improve delivery of PublicDigit; every iteration produces measurable progress on a PublicDigit feature; platform-only iterations are exceptional and require explicit ARB approval' — ADOPTED. M-B (Product Discovery Charter), 'there is a market for an AI-native Knowledge Operating System for software engineering whose core promise is preserving architectural knowledge, enforcing engineering governance, and enabling AI agents to reason consistently across complex software systems' — PROPOSED, UNAPPROVED, explicitly a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The mission, as adopted ... KnowledgeOS exists to improve the delivery of PublicDigit by governing how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified and evolved — in a form that is independent of project, programming language and execution provider
b_rows_sample.statement: The adopted mission combines two observed halves: the purpose from AIP-14 (improve delivery of PublicDigit) and the form from the Reference Architecture section 1 (governs how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified, and evolved, independent of project, programming language, or execution provider). The apparent contradiction between 'solely for PublicDigit' and 'independent of project' is resolved: AIP-14 constrains WHY work is undertaken, the Reference Architecture constrains WHAT is built — build portable things only when doing so advances this product; AIP-14's enforcement is an iteration-cost metric and an over-evolution review, a cost control, not a scope boundary. M-B is a different mission with a different customer ('organizations' rather than 'the engineering team'), not adopted, gate shut.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Part 2 — Responsibilities (R-1..R-8)
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight responsibilities, each traced to an artifact: R-1 govern the engineering lifecycle (EEP); R-2 hold the authority model (ES-001); R-3 hold the method (Round39-MC, Round47-OP, workbooks); R-4 define the shape of a capability (Platform_Capability_Pattern FROZEN, PGP-01..05); R-5 make governed knowledge retrievable and enforceable (Knowledge-Constitution, 18 lint rules, portal); R-6 harvest reusable knowledge from operational evidence (ES-006.4/ES-006.1 — the responsibility exists, but 0 traversals); R-7 keep runtime vocabulary out of governance (asserted, artifact missing); R-8 refuse to approve its own work (EEP: automation does not approve itself).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3 — Non-responsibilities (N-1..N-10) ... N-1 is breached today. Recording the breach is this document's act; repairing it is not
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten non-responsibilities, each traced: N-1 business/domain knowledge (elections, voters, adjudication) — BREACHED: ES-005.1 names PublicDigit and hard-codes .claude/; N-2 a product's evidence records; N-3 any register's contents (only the governing rule); N-4 a runtime's vocabulary; N-5 its own approval; N-6 governance defined by automation; N-7 duplicated knowledge (ES-005.4); N-8 materialized consolidations (BRM-1 retired extraction-by-copy); N-9 a product's PKS; N-10 orchestrators/workflow engines/state machines (Reference Architecture section 1: deliberately, and not forever, until operational evidence demonstrates insufficiency). N-1's breach is recorded but not repaired here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-1 | Which mission governs — M-A (adopted, PublicDigit-serving) or M-B (proposed, product-seeking)?
b_rows_sample.statement: MQ-1: which mission governs, M-A or M-B — they have different customers and are not reconcilable by drafting — authority: sponsor + DA.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-2..MQ-7 | Who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole? ... Is N-1's breach to be repaired ... Is PD-3's individual ownership intentional ... is the harvest responsibility even required ... Does N-10 still hold ... What would falsify M-A?
b_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The finding ... KnowledgeOS has TWO missions. One is adopted; the other is what everyone has been designing for ... Almost every architectural difficulty in this track is a symptom of designing under M-B while governed by M-A
b_rows_sample.statement: The document's headline finding (before its own later withdrawal, recorded above): almost every architectural difficulty in the track is a symptom of designing under M-B (organizations as customers) while governed by M-A (serve PublicDigit): under M-A, extraction is premature and 'knowledgeos init' is out of mission, while under M-B they are the goal/the product; under M-A the harvest loop is optional (MQ-5) while under M-B it is essential; under M-A 'no second adopting product' is not a gap while under M-B it is the blocker; under M-A platform-only iterations need ARB approval while under M-B they are normal work. MQ-1 is not a documentation question — until answered, the same evidence supports opposite conclusions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — D-9 · Derive the Platform Cost metric; run the AIP-14 over-evolution check (FIRST — it gates the docket itself)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 1 (D-9): compute the AIP-14 Platform Cost metric for recent iterations and rule whether the over-evolution review fires, since the tripwire cannot fire if the metric is never computed. Supporting: ~48h produced 20+ platform-only documents and zero PublicDigit feature progress in this track (self-declared). Opposing: dense real product delivery ran in parallel; the platform work was commissioned, not drift. Downstream: whether Packages 2-10 are worked now at all. Authority: ARB. Recommendation: ADOPT, run the check before anything else on this docket.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — AMENDMENT (REV 2): the metric must be DEFINED before it is RUN ... D-9 therefore splits into D-9a (DEFINE) and D-9b (RUN)
b_rows_sample.statement: A PA review challenge is accepted: should AIP-14 measure platform work by document count, engineering effort, elapsed time, or delivered capability, since document count can be misleading? This corrects the docket's own defect: Package 1's supporting-evidence line presupposed document count as the metric, exactly the undecided question — that line is downgraded from trigger evidence to illustration pending metric definition. D-9 splits: D-9a defines the Platform Cost measurement basis (recommend delivered-capability + effort, reject raw document count, since one strategic decision may produce many small governance documents while a large implementation may produce few); D-9b runs the over-evolution check using the defined basis, immediately after D-9a. Package 1 stays first on the docket; what changed is that the gate must be built before it can be closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 2 — D-5 · Ratify the enacted mission (one signature; unblocks the frame)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 2 (D-5): ratify (or amend and ratify) the mission the machinery already enacts ('provide a reusable engineering platform that improves the development of software systems through governed engineering knowledge'). Supporting: ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest, the pre-positioned Platform=Adoption split, blind convergence A-1/A-2. Risk of adopting is low; risk of rejecting is that the vacancy keeps pulling constraints upward into mission-shaped misreadings. Authority: sponsor. Recommendation: ADOPT.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — "VACANT" WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME I HAVE MADE THIS EXACT ERROR ... ARTIFACT ABSENCE ≠ CONCEPT ABSENCE
b_rows_sample.statement: A recurring error pattern is named: artifact absence != concept absence — looking for a document, not finding one, and declaring the concept missing. Three instances: (1) 'there is no strategic-DDD method' (it existed, unindexed); (2) 'there is no capability pattern' (it existed, FROZEN); (3) 'the Mission layer is vacant' (it exists, implicit, enacted in machinery). Strategic DDD asks why a system exists, not whether a document titled Mission Statement exists — Linux and PostgreSQL have no mission statements and unmistakable missions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE OBJECTION IS UPHELD, AND MY ERROR IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN "WRONG FRAMING" ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION, then reported a conflict between a constraint and a hypothesis — which are not comparable things
b_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's objection is upheld with a more specific diagnosis: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission, then reported as conflicting with a hypothesis (M-B), which are not comparable categories. The document's own prior text already disproved the label, calling AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after calling it a mission — both cannot be true.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-canonical-essence' POSSIBLY relates to 'mission' (batch B0006). Note: The ratified one-sentence KnowledgeOS definition ('a constitutional epistemic operating system that enables trustworthy truth discovery by preserving the identity, context, evidence, reasoning, uncertainty, agency, and historical evolution of knowledge across time'), the latest head of an essence-refinement chain; may be the same object as the already-registered 'mission' (KnowledgeOS purpose layer) at a later revision, or a distinct downstream artifact -- not stated as an alias in this file group.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance → Evidence → Knowledge → Assurance → External Engineering Systems
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a preliminary context-mapping relationship chain (Governance consumes evidence -> Evidence supports -> Knowledge defines expectation -> Assurance observes engineering reality -> External Engineering Systems), noting the actual dependency direction must eventually be verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ExternalModel → Translation → KnowledgeOSModel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires an anti-corruption layer when KnowledgeOS consumes external engineering state — it should not adopt the external system's language wholesale (e.g. Kubernetes 'Deployment ReplicaSet status' -> KnowledgeOS 'observed deployment state'; Nexus repository/blob store/component/asset/version -> NexusAsset->ArtifactObservation); likewise Claude's internal concepts (conversation, token, tool call, context window) are not KnowledgeOS domain concepts — KnowledgeOS needs AgentSession only where agent activity has governance/evidence significance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance → Knowledge → {Assurance, Evidence} → External Engineering Systems/Runtime ← Agent Layer
a_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams a candidate context map (Governance->Knowledge->{Assurance,Evidence}->External Engineering Systems/Runtime, with an Agent Layer feeding in), explicitly still a hypothesis; concludes the key DDD insight that KnowledgeOS may not be one bounded context but an 'ecosystem of bounded contexts' connected by a common governance/evidence language (KnowledgeOS = BC1+BC2+BC3+Integration, not one huge application), though it might alternatively be primarily a platform boundary spanning several domains — a distinction to be resolved by implementation/ownership evidence, not assumed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeProposed, KnowledgeApproved, DecisionSuperseded, EvidenceCaptured, FindingDetected, FindingClassified, ActionAuthorized, ActionExecuted, VerificationCompleted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes nine candidate domain events as potential integration events, and the DDD event-ownership rule: 'the context that owns the business meaning should own the event' (e.g. Governance->DecisionApproved, not a generic KnowledgeOS GenericEventService->DecisionApproved); assembles an event-driven control-loop choreography (Governance-DecisionApproved->Knowledge->ExpectedState->Assurance-FindingDetected->Governance-ActionAuthorized->Engineering->Verification); explicitly warns the semantic event model does not imply Kafka/messaging/webhooks as implementation — DomainEvent is preserved as the semantic concept, independent of mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance → Knowledge → Assurance → Engineering ... Infrastructure/Agent → Authority
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 128 (Context Map and Dependency Direction): will construct the KnowledgeOS Context Map and determine actual dependency direction, testing whether it follows Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering or contains reverse dependencies/semantic leakage; specifically flags the dangerous anti-pattern Infrastructure/Agent -> Authority, which would mean technical implementation could silently redefine organizational truth; previews deliverables (upstream/downstream relationships, published language, anti-corruption layers, shared kernels, dependency direction, agent integration boundary, external-system boundaries, first candidate DDD architecture fitness rules).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority → Knowledge → Assurance → Engineering → Observation → Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Context Map's purpose is to determine where semantic authority is located and which direction knowledge/dependencies may flow, aiming to prevent the dangerous inversion Technical implementation -> Organizational authority in favor of Authority->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering->Observation->Evidence with feedback through governed mechanisms; presents the full candidate context-map diagram (Governance[Policy/Decision] -governs/authorizes-> Knowledge[Claims/Facts] -expected state-> Assurance[Rules/Checks] -verifies-> Engineering/Runtime/External Systems -observations-> Evidence -supports-> back to Knowledge), explicitly a target hypothesis, not current-state fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance → Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Justifies each context-map edge: Governance->Knowledge (governance establishes what is organizationally binding, e.g. Architecture Decision->Authoritative Knowledge, Governance Policy->Applicable Constraint, Approved Exception->Effective Expected State; governance must not depend on an agent's interpretation to become authoritative); Knowledge->Assurance (knowledge translates governance into reusable engineering meaning, e.g. Decision D42 establishing 'Service X must use pattern P' becomes an assurance expectation, so assurance consumes the authoritative expectation rather than inventing it); Assurance->EngineeringState (assurance observes/evaluates engineering reality but does not own it); Engineering->Evidence (Runtime->Observation->Evidence, e.g. Git commit/CI result/deployed image/Kubernetes state/monitoring/security scan, with KnowledgeOS preserving references/interpretation without becoming the source system); Evidence->Knowledge (Evidence->Claim is valid, but Evidence ↛ Authority automatically — 'one of the central boundaries'), closing the semantic feedback loop Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering->Evidence->Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance owns Detection; Governance owns Disposition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolves where Finding belongs: Assurance owns Detection (Assurance->FindingDetected), Governance owns Disposition (Finding->Governance), avoiding mixing technical verification with organizational decision-making; gives the Finding lifecycle Assurance->FindingDetected->Classification->Governance->{Remediate, AcceptRisk, Exception, Investigate, FalsePositive}, noting classification may be partly automated but must follow governed rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence as an owned semantic context with explicit contracts ... not a Shared Kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against making Evidence a large Shared Kernel across Governance/Knowledge/Assurance/Engineering (creates coupling); prefers Evidence as an owned context consumed by others through references/projections; if a shared kernel is used at all it should be extremely small — potentially only Identity+Reference+Version+ProvenanceMetadata, never the entire Knowledge domain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceDecisionApproved, GovernanceExceptionGranted, KnowledgePublished, EvidenceCaptured, FindingDetected, VerificationCompleted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate Published Language (named integration-event contracts) whose importance is that the contract carries meaning, not merely technical DTOs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kubernetes Deployment → Kubernetes Adapter → Runtime Observation (not Kubernetes object model → KnowledgeOS domain model directly)
a_rows_sample.statement: Elaborates the Anti-Corruption Layer requirement with worked examples: Kubernetes Deployment -> Adapter -> Runtime Observation (not a direct object-model mapping); Nexus Repository/Blob Store/Component/Asset/Version -> Adapter -> KnowledgeOS Artifact/ArtifactVersion/ArtifactObservation; Git commit/branch/tag/repository/merge -> Commit->ImplementationEvidence without redefining Git's domain; CI 'Pipeline #842 passed' -> VerificationEvidence while the CI system remains authority for its own execution (KnowledgeOS ≠ CI/CD).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → Context Projection → AI Agent → {Analysis, Tools→{Git,CI,Runtime}}
a_rows_sample.statement: Places Claude/Codex at the application/integration layer, consuming governed context and producing evidence/recommendations/actions; states the agent must not become an upstream context (Agent ↛ Governance meaning 'agent determines governance truth' is forbidden; correct is Agent->Recommendation->Governance, agent downstream from authority); requires a recommendation to carry producedBy=Agent, basedOn=Evidence, proposedFor=Decision, making the AI contribution explicit without granting authority; both Claude and Codex should consume the same KnowledgeOSContext (Context Contract) even though harnesses differ operationally, giving the correct symmetry SameKnowledgeAuthority+SameEvidenceDiscipline+SameGovernanceBoundary+SameActionConstraints, explicitly not SameConfigurationFiles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Technical contexts must not define organizational authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formulates the dependency-direction rule (Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering, with evidence flowing back Engineering->Observation->Evidence->Knowledge/Governance) and three named forbidden-dependency anti-patterns: (1) Runtime->'current reality'->automatically authoritative knowledge->Governance is forbidden because observation ('what is') does not establish organizational intent ('what should be'); (2) Agent->Inference->Authoritative Architecture is forbidden, correct is Agent->Inference->Evidence->Validation->Governance->Authority; (3) Assurance->Violation->automatic policy change is forbidden, correct is Assurance->Finding->Governance->Decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance→Knowledge: Upstream/Downstream; Knowledge→Assurance: Published Language; Assurance→External Systems: Customer/Supplier; External Systems→Evidence: Supplier; Evidence→Knowledge: Published Evidence Contract.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assigns classic DDD context-map relationship types per edge, explicitly hypotheses pending implementation confirmation; tabulates candidate context ownership (Governance: Architecture/Governance authority; Knowledge: KnowledgeOS/domain owner; Evidence: KnowledgeOS/evidence capability owner; Assurance: Engineering/architecture assurance; Runtime: Operational system owner; Agent: AI engineering platform; IAM: Enterprise security/IAM), stating without ownership a bounded context is merely a technical grouping — the next reconstruction phase must inspect repositories, teams, deployment ownership, project tracking, APIs, docs, and architecture decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority flows downward; evidence flows upward.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 128 verdict and resulting architecture principle: the emerging context map Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering with Engineering->Observation->Evidence->Knowledge, external systems (Runtime/Git/Nexus/CI-CD/IAM) remaining authoritative for their own domains, Claude/Codex as agent/application integration contexts, and the core contexts remaining Governance/Knowledge/Evidence/Assurance; boxed principle 'authority flows downward; evidence flows upward' (Authority->ExpectedState->Engineering while Engineering->Observation->Evidence->Governance, meeting in assurance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: RaiseFinding can trigger GovernanceDispositionRequested; Assurance should not directly mutate Governance state (Event → GovernanceApplicationService).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines cross-context commands (one context's command triggering another's workflow via events routed through the target context's application service, never direct state mutation) and three context-integration patterns: synchronous query (current knowledge retrieval, Agent->KnowledgeQuery), command (state-changing request, Agent->ActionRequest), domain event (asynchronous propagation, VerificationCompleted->FindingProcess); warns against event-driven-everything — a query like 'what rules apply to Nexus?' needs no RuleQueryRequestedEvent, since events are for propagating state-change facts, not every interaction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: How can KnowledgeOS connect Governance, Knowledge, Evidence, Assurance, Agents, Git, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Nexus without allowing any of them to become the accidental owner of another context's semantics?
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 139 (Context Map & Integration Contracts): defines upstream/downstream relationships, query/command/event classification, translation points, Anti-Corruption Layer placement, and Assurance-Graph-as-projection placement, to produce the first formal KnowledgeOS Context Map.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context Map + Explicit Contracts + Controlled Translation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central DDD question ('how do independently owned models cooperate without sharing or corrupting each other's semantics?') and presents the full context-map diagram plus a nine-row upstream/downstream relationship table (Governance->Knowledge: Published language/governed contract; Governance->Assurance: Policy/rule derivation; Knowledge->Assurance: Conformity input; Engineering->Evidence: Observation capture; Evidence->Knowledge: Evidence-backed claims; Assurance->Governance: Findings/disposition; KnowledgeOS->Agents: Open host service/API; Agents->Engineering: Tool/action contract; External systems->KnowledgeOS: Anti-Corruption Layer), explicitly architectural hypotheses pending implementation validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GovernanceEvent → KnowledgeConsumer. DecisionID/DecisionStatus/Scope/Validity/PolicyReferences as a candidate Published Language.
a_rows_sample.statement: Details Governance->Knowledge: DecisionApproved can result in KnowledgeExpectationUpdated, but Governance must not directly manipulate Knowledge's internal model — a candidate Published Language contract is proposed that does not share internal domain objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy ≠ Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Details Governance->Assurance (Policy P42->FitnessRule R17; Assurance receives ApplicableRuleDefinition but owns Verification) with the separation 'Governance says this must be true, Assurance says we checked whether it is true, therefore Policy ≠ Verification'; details Knowledge->Assurance with a worked example (Knowledge: ApprovedNexusVersion=3.70 vs Observed=3.69).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, FORMALIZE, CONNECT, CONSTRAIN, INTRODUCE, RETIRE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 143 (Current -> Target Architecture Delta): defines seven delta-transformation categories to classify every capability, producing 'what KnowledgeOS actually needs to build' rather than another abstract architecture, and previews Step 144's KnowledgeOS Evolution Roadmap (Current Platform -> Target Architecture) with explicit work packages and sequencing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, FORMALIZE, CONNECT, CONSTRAIN, INTRODUCE, RETIRE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the seven delta transformation types and presents the master delta map across 19 architecture areas (repository agent integration KEEP+CONSTRAIN; .claude/.codex CONSTRAIN; AGENTS.md KEEP+FORMALIZE; agent memory CONSTRAIN; governance artifacts/architecture knowledge FORMALIZE; registry STRENGTHEN; deterministic checks CONNECT+FORMALIZE; session logging CONNECT; evidence FORMALIZE+CONNECT; verification/findings FORMALIZE; cross-context relationships INTRODUCE; governed context FORMALIZE+CONNECT; authorization STRENGTHEN; external systems CONSTRAIN; auditability CONNECT; temporal knowledge FORMALIZE) — the core transformation map, with the transformation framed as Existing mechanisms -> Explicit semantic contracts -> Governed engineering system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Object schema; AuthorityType = f(Context, ClaimType) — not AUTHORITATIVE > EVERYTHING.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 3 (Establish Knowledge Authority), one of the highest-priority changes: a Knowledge Object schema (identity, type, source, authority, status, validity, provenance, relationships) and a seven-level authority classification (AUTHORITATIVE, VERIFIED, OBSERVED, DERIVED, PROPOSED, LOCAL, UNKNOWN) explicitly not a linear ranking — corrects a simplistic 'AUTHORITATIVE > everything' view with AuthorityType=f(Context,ClaimType), e.g. Kubernetes authoritative for current pod state, Governance for organizational policy, Git for repository history, KnowledgeOS for governed claim lifecycle; each authority type is strongest within its own dimension (e.g. OBSERVED can outrank DERIVED for runtime state).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Existing Document → Governance Object → Relationships → Document Projection. Draft→Review→Approve→Effective→Supersede.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 4 (Formalize Governance): reverses the document/knowledge relationship so the document becomes a representation of governed knowledge rather than the sole record, with a target machine-addressable governance lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: check_nexus_version.sh → Rule: NEXUS_VERSION_COMPLIANCE; Checker = Implementation. Rule → Policy → Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 5 (Formalize Rules): gives existing deterministic checks stable rule identities separate from their script implementation, with a Rule schema (ID, version, description, scope, severity, applicability, expected state, checker reference, governance source) enabling Rule->Policy->Decision traceability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verification(V42) against Rule(R17:v3) which implements Policy(P8) established by Decision(D42) — a governance-grade assertion instead of 'Nexus check failed.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 6 (Connect Checks to Governance): transforms Check->PASS/FAIL into Decision->Policy->Rule->Checker->Verification, worked with the Nexus example, giving results organizational meaning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceID with Source/CapturedAt/CapturedBy/Subject/Integrity/Provenance. Git commit ← Evidence Reference ← KnowledgeOS (evidence federation, not full duplication).
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 7 (Formalize Evidence): a common evidence-record schema and evidence federation (referencing rather than centralizing raw data).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent=Codex, Session=S182, Recommendation=R44, Action=A91, Commit=abc123, Evidence=E77.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 8 (Connect Session Logging): evolves existing session/change logging into AgentSession->Action->Evidence with a worked full-identity-chain example, 'far stronger than a free-form session log.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision -governs-> Policy -implementedBy-> Rule -verifiedBy-> Verification -supportedBy-> Evidence. Graph = Projection, not MasterDatabase.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 9 (Introduce the Assurance Graph), 'the largest genuinely new architectural capability': makes relationships explicit via named node identities (DEC-42, POL-17, RULE-91, VER-182) and named edge semantics (governs, supports, evaluates, implementedBy, authorizedBy, producedBy — far better than generic 'relatedTo'), restating the graph must be treated as Projection, not MasterDatabase.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Task → Context Service {Governance, Knowledge, Evidence, Assurance, Graph, Authorization} → Context Package → Agent. Action → ContextID.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 10 (Introduce Governed Context Service): the Context Service becomes the primary KnowledgeOS-Agent interface (Task->Relevant governed context), with every context package carrying a ContextID so an action can reference it and later reconstruction is possible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ValidFrom/ValidUntil as first-class concepts. A(t2) needs Context(t2), not Context(now).
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 12 (Introduce Temporal Semantics): distinguishes 'what is true now' from 'what was considered true when this action happened,' essential for audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EXPECTATION → RULE → CHECK → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → FINDING → DISPOSITION → EXPECTATION. The loop is more important than the graph.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 14 (Build the Assurance Loop): the operational heart of KnowledgeOS, emphasizing 'closed-loop engineering assurance' is the real capability — the graph merely makes the loop navigable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Finding → Disposition: Remediate, Accept Risk, Grant Exception, Change Policy, False Positive, Investigate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 15 (Establish Finding Disposition): a failed check must not simply disappear into a report but reach one of six governance-owned disposition outcomes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentCapability ≠ Authorization. Deploy capability does not imply MayDeploy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 16 (Separate Human and Agent Authority): restates capability≠authorization must hold both technically and semantically.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Domain → Port → Adapter → External System. GitPort, NexusPort, KubernetesPort.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 18 (External-System Boundary): moves existing integrations conceptually behind ports so replacing e.g. Nexus only changes NexusAdapter->NewAdapter while the Assurance domain remains unchanged.

b_rows_sample.anchor: GraphProjectionHealthy, EvidenceIntegrityHealthy, OutboxHealthy, AuthorizationHealthy, ContextGenerationHealthy. KnowledgeOS → assures → KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 19 (Platform Self-Assurance): KnowledgeOS should eventually verify its own architectural integrity via named deterministic self-health checks.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule 1: One authoritative owner per semantic concept. ... Rule 7: Derived projections must be rebuildable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Work Package 20 (Architecture Constitution): proposes capturing the discovered architectural rules as a formal KnowledgeOS Architecture Constitution (seven numbered rules consolidating one-authoritative-owner, no cross-context mutation, agent-local non-authority, governed authorization, deterministic-verification-preference, provenance-awareness, and projection-rebuildability), to become architectural fitness rules; diagrams the resulting recursion KnowledgeOS Architecture->Architecture Rules->Assurance Checkers->KnowledgeOS Verification->KnowledgeOS Architecture Health — 'the platform can therefore verify conformance to its own architecture.'

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['kos', 'map', 'preview'])
