b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

a_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
a_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
a_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
a_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
a_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 5 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status(I) in {Implemented, Partial, Specified, Missing, Unknown} ... Unknown != Missing ... Unknown != Implemented
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-value implementation-status classification for every architectural property (Implemented/Partial/Specified/Missing/Unknown), with boxed guardrails Unknown!=Missing and Unknown!=Implemented -- the distinction between Missing and Unknown is called critical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We derive a good architectural principle and gradually begin speaking about it as though the existing system already implements it. That would be architectural hallucination ... Derived Architecture != Current Architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the risk of 'architectural hallucination' -- gradually treating a derived architectural principle as though the existing system already implements it -- and sets a strict boundary Derived Architecture != Current Architecture, requiring the current architecture to be established from evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_i=(I_i,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a per-invariant evidence record G_i=(Invariant,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap) as the unit of the architecture audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I1 Identity ≠ State ... I15 No silent semantic strengthening ... none of these should yet be marked 'Implemented' merely because we derived them
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists a first 15-item theoretical assurance register (I1-I15: Identity!=State, historical version preservation, provenance preservation, epistemic status preservation, Unknown!=False, uncertainty preservation, model-version integrity, Inference!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, contradiction preservation, temporal validity, legal state transitions, pre/postconditions, no silent semantic strengthening), explicitly marked as targets not yet verified as implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_0=No evidence ... E_5=Formal verification
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-level evidence-quality hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E5 (formal verification), via E1 claim/documentation, E2 static implementation evidence, E3 executable test evidence, E4 runtime/production evidence, worked through a provenance example progressing from documentation claim to automated evidence-chain test to production lineage recording.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I)
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates evidence strength from confidence: strong (E2) evidence from inspecting only one module may still leave confidence in system-wide enforcement low; Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture is 82% compliant ... unless we have first defined ... population ... weighting ... independence ... evidence quality ... confidence model ... treatment of critical properties
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against stating an unsupported compliance percentage (e.g. '82% compliant') without first defining the requirement population, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model and treatment of critical properties; recommends a qualitative CriticalGap measure instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 — Semantic gap ... G5 — Assurance gap ... These gaps can coexist
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five coexisting gap classes: G1 Semantic (software loses domain meaning), G2 Governance (authority/responsibility ambiguous), G3 Temporal (historical state not reconstructable), G4 Epistemic (evidence/uncertainty/assumptions lost), G5 Assurance (behavior may be correct but insufficiently evidenced).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation = Present but Assurance = Weak. This is not necessarily an implementation gap. It is an: Assurance Gap
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example distinguishing implementation presence from assurance: modelVersion correctly stored (Implementation=Present) but with no automated test proving it survives the workflow (Assurance=Weak) is classified specifically as an Assurance Gap, not an implementation gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Architecture gap (design itself lacks the mechanism), Implementation gap (mechanism specified but code does not implement it correctly), and Verification gap (implementation appears correct but evidence is insufficient) as three non-identical gap types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing ... Ownerless Invariants ... Shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a governance gap pattern where a technical mechanism (AI->Assessment->Approval) works but nobody has defined who is authorized to approve, so TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing; introduces the 'ownerless invariant' search (Owner(I)=empty set, dangerous because nobody maintains it) and its converse, the 'shared ownership' problem, where undivided shared responsibility (Owner(I)={A,B,C}) risks each team assuming another enforces the invariant -- boxed as 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) ... Loss(C)={p | p in CriticalProperties and p absent after transformation}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-loss function for a context-to-context contract L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C), refined to Loss(C) as the set of critical properties absent after transformation; worked example: an Assessment=(score,uncertainty,modelVersion,evidenceRef) contract sending only {score} loses uncertainty/modelVersion/evidenceRef, a Critical Semantic Gap if downstream governance requires them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ΔT=T_target △ T_actual where △ denotes symmetric difference ... Unauthorized State Transition Path
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing actual state-machine transitions T_actual from implementation and comparing to target transitions T_target via symmetric difference DeltaT = T_target triangle T_actual as a state-transition gap measure; a transition present in T_actual but absent from T_target is an Unauthorized State Transition Path warranting high priority when governance consequences exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t) ... Reproducibility ... Replayability ... A system may be replayable without being perfectly reproducible
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines historical replay Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t), noting exact replay (Replay(A,t)=A_t) may be impossible when external conditions change, in which case the system should preserve enough provenance to explain why; distinguishes Reproducibility (can we regenerate the same result, F(X,M)=Y again) from Replayability (can we reconstruct what happened and why), noting a system may be replayable without being reproducible (e.g. a now-defunct external service).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A new state does not necessarily know the old state ... CurrentState + HistoricalProvenance ... History must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a technically disciplined reading of an earlier 'Chapter 4' observation ('a new state does not necessarily know the old state'): rejects CurrentState=History, proposing instead CurrentState+HistoricalProvenance as sufficient for reconstructing relevant prior meaning; boxed principle: history must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prediction -> AutomaticAuthority ... CurrentState -> AssumeCompleteHistory ... Unknown -> False ... Execution -> AssumeSuccess ... Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions
a_rows_sample.statement: States a negative-space design principle: a mature architecture must specify ForbiddenPaths as well as AllowedPaths (Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions), and lists four named forbidden implicit transitions to guard against: Prediction->AutomaticAuthority, CurrentState->AssumeCompleteHistory, Unknown->False, Execution->AssumeSuccess.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 Identity ... G-15 History ... This is the audit instrument
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 15-item provisional gap register (G-01 through G-15) as concrete audit questions (identity/state separation, historical reconstructability, provenance traceability, uncertainty preservation across boundaries, model/version provenance, inference-to-authority escalation, decision/execution separation, execution/outcome separation, illegal transition blocking, contract semantic loss, contradiction coexistence, unknown-vs-false distinguishability, automatic critical-invariant testing, single accountable ownership, prior semantic context reconstruction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No evidence => Unknown. Not: No evidence => Missing. And certainly not: No evidence => Implemented
a_rows_sample.statement: States the methodological rule of Step 212 as most important: the gap register's rows must not be populated by imagination but from actual KnowledgeOS artifacts, with the default for absence of evidence being No evidence=>Unknown, explicitly not =>Missing and certainly not =>Implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Architectural reasoning PASS ... Gītā Chapters 1–4 COHERENT
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 verdict: architectural reasoning, DDD, mathematics, statistics, and AI dimensions each rated PASS; Gita chapters 1-4 rated COHERENT (continuing to generate architectural questions without being presented as technical proof).

b_rows_sample.anchor: F | D | P | U ... F = Fact ... D = Derived ... P = Proposed ... U = Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way epistemic classification for every architectural statement: F=Fact (directly supported by engineering evidence), D=Derived (logically derived from facts/observations), P=Proposed (a recommendation or future design), U=Unknown (insufficient evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We designed the system according to this architecture from the beginning ... That would be misleading. The intellectually stronger story is: Experience -> Problem -> Observation -> Experiment -> Pattern -> Abstraction -> Theory -> Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against retrospectively rewriting the book's history as if the system had been designed according to the derived architecture from the beginning, calling this misleading; proposes instead the causal chain Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture as the intellectually stronger and more honest narrative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How can this artifact support our current theory? We should ask: What does this artifact actually establish?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the archaeological method's central mindset shift: treat prior artifacts (prompts, AI outputs, architecture docs, ADRs, code, tests, rejected ideas, contradictions, revisions) as evidence to be asked 'what does this actually establish', never 'how does this support our current theory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions} ... Artifact -> Evidence -> Interpretation. Not: Theory -> selective evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence extraction per artifact E(A_j) as the set {Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}, to be connected to architectural concepts only afterward (Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation), explicitly rejecting the reverse flow Theory->selective evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence ... unless we have evidence of absence
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that absence of knowledge about whether a property (e.g. provenance) exists in an implementation be written as Unknown ('could not yet be established from the available evidence'), never as an assertion of absence ('is missing') unless positive evidence of absence exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(C)={A_1,A_2,...,A_n} ... provenance of architecture itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes giving architectural claims themselves a provenance set Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n} of supporting artifacts, so a reader can trace Claim->Evidence -- termed 'provenance of architecture itself'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADL = Decision -> Problem -> Evidence -> Alternatives -> Rationale -> Consequence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Architecture Decision Lineage ADL = Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence, proposed to eventually become part of the KnowledgeOS architecture itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Failure -> Knowledge ... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches ... What did not work ... alongside ... What eventually worked. Otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable
b_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-result principle: a failed experiment (Hypothesis H tested, Result=not-H) is Failure->Knowledge, not useless, and some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches; the book should explicitly record what did not work alongside what eventually worked, because otherwise the final architecture looks falsely inevitable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ChosenPattern ... RejectedPattern ... ReasonForRejection
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects the negative-result principle to the corpus's Chapter 4 theme: knowledge includes discrimination between Valid and Invalid, so the architecture should preserve not only the ChosenPattern but sometimes the RejectedPattern and ReasonForRejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The strongest new result is actually the dependency-cycle finding ... three dependency cycles, all through one node ... the bootstrap boundary is 𝒪/𝒯 ratification ... But—and this is critical—**the report must not turn that observation into a recommendation to ratify a particular 𝒪 or 𝒯.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Elevates Step 288's dependency-cycle finding (three cycles, all through one node, with the bootstrap boundary claimed to be O/T ratification) above the 32-relations result as the programme's most important new result, reframing the problem from 'define equality' to a cyclic dependency diagram among equality, identity, operations, semantics, transformations, and observability with one governance-dependent bootstrap point -- while explicitly cautioning that identifying O/T as the bootstrap node must not be turned into a recommendation for what O or T should actually be (that belongs to Governance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 288 has **not** established: the meaning of `≡`; ... the operation set `𝒪`; transformation semantics `𝒯`; ... the canonical implementation representation. So the next step should **not** be another broad "solve equality" step.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates twelve things Step 288 explicitly has NOT established (the meanings of equiv, equiv_K, approx, cong_lambda; whether Pi is in equiv; the observation set; the operational kernel; the operation set O; transformation semantics T; state identity; equality/congruence compatibility with operations; equality compatibility with delta; the canonical implementation representation), concluding the next step must not be another broad 'solve equality' step, which would repeat the same mistake at a higher level; instead Step 289 should be a dependency-and-bootstrap resolution step asking what can be derived, what requires governance, and what must remain blocked because the dependency graph is cyclic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every directed dependency A → B state exactly what B needs from A. Do not infer dependencies merely because two concepts are mentioned in the same document. ... classified as: CORPUS / DERIVED / EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED / INTERPRETATION / NORMATIVE / TECHNICALLY OPEN / UNKNOWN
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that Step 289's dependency graph be built only from genuine definitional or operational dependencies, never mere textual co-occurrence, with every directed edge A->B stating exactly what B needs from A and classified into one of seven evidence classes (CORPUS, DERIVED, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, INTERPRETATION, NORMATIVE, TECHNICALLY OPEN, UNKNOWN); requires the three Step-288 cycles to be independently reconstructed (not assumed correct) with edge-level evidence and stress-tested against deletion of philosophical, verification-lane, and historical/non-normative material.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determine whether this is: A. FORMALLY PROVEN B. DERIVED BUT CONDITIONAL C. STRONGLY SUPPORTED D. AN ARCHITECTURAL INTERPRETATION E. NORMATIVE F. NOT ESTABLISHED ... Find the minimal cut set. ... Do not preselect the answer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires an explicit, six-way classification (formally proven / derived-but-conditional / strongly supported / architectural interpretation / normative / not established) of the specific claim 'O/T ratification is the bootstrap boundary', and requires the minimal cut set breaking all dependency cycles to be found by actual search over the reconstructed graph rather than preselected or assumed to be {O/T} -- explicitly floating the possibility that the true minimal set could be {O/T}, {O/T, Pi-in-equiv}, or some other set, to be derived, not guessed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create a reusable mathematical-audit rule: Before accepting any property from a finite exhaustive test, check whether the tested relation is: universal, empty, singleton, identity, degenerate along one or more axes, or otherwise incapable of meaningfully exercising the property. Apply this rule retrospectively to all major equality/observability results in Steps 287–288.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates promoting the zero-transitivity-violations incident into a formal, reusable degeneracy-audit rule (before accepting any exhaustively-tested property, check whether the tested relation is universal, empty, singleton, identity, or otherwise degenerate) and requires this rule to be applied RETROSPECTIVELY to every major equality/observability result across Steps 287-288, with any result needing downgrading to be explicitly identified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use only the following status classes: ESTABLISHED BOUNDED DERIVED EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED CORROBORATED NORMATIVE TECHNICALLY OPEN G1 DEFERRED REFUTED SUPERSEDED INTERPRETATION Do not use: CLOSED unless a specific closure contract has actually been satisfied.
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixes a twelve-item closed status vocabulary for Step 289 (ESTABLISHED, BOUNDED, DERIVED, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, CORROBORATED, NORMATIVE, TECHNICALLY OPEN, G1, DEFERRED, REFUTED, SUPERSEDED, INTERPRETATION), explicitly forbidding the word CLOSED unless a specific, stated closure contract has actually been satisfied; also mandates that the Step-286 philosophical programme not participate in the core dependency derivation (the result must survive with the philosophical appendix deleted, with any philosophical corroboration stated only separately).

a_rows_sample.anchor: STOP. Do not proceed to Step 290. Do not draft an implementation design. Do not recommend a canonical equality relation. Do not recommend an operational kernel. a_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit stop condition closing the mandate: Step 289 must not proceed to Step 290, must not draft an implementation design, and must not recommend a canonical equality relation, operational kernel, O, or T -- its sole purpose is to establish the exact boundary between what research can determine and what must be decided elsewhere, closing with the required final sentence that Step 289 establishes the dependency/bootstrap boundary but ratifies none of the equality contract, operation model, transformation model, or operational kernel.

b_rows_sample.statement: After removing the spurious K<->equiv_T edge, the corrected 27-node/42-edge graph has exactly 4 elementary cycles, all passing through the node 'equiv' (semantic equality): approx<->equiv; congruence<->equiv; approx->equiv->bindings->approx; congruence->equiv->delta->congruence. b_rows_sample.statement: Reconstructs the KnowledgeOS equality/kernel dependency graph as an explicit, cited edge list (27 nodes spanning O, T, O_K, equiv, approx, delta, congruence, minimality, K, equiv_T, identity, id_context, Pi, bindings, canonicalization, struct_eq, evidence, merge, state_rep, invariants, sufficiency, kernel, assertion, temporal, Qualify, projection, policy), with every edge A->B meaning 'B needs A' and carrying an explicit corpus or derivation citation (e.g. O->T cites Step 259; equiv->delta is DERIVED; approx->equiv cites the 261.5/261.21 formula collision, i.e. the N-1 conflict) -- explicitly excluding co-occurrence-only relationships as edges, per the mandate's requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RESOLVABLE = { "O": ("NORMATIVE", ...), "T": ("NORMATIVE", ...), "O_K": ("NORMATIVE", "261.21: 'O_K is not yet completely closed'"), "equiv": ("NORMATIVE", "N-1 conflict + Decision 3; 012 s35: not fully decidable"), "delta": ("NORMATIVE", "transformation semantics; commit case unspecifiable"), ... "Qualify": ("G1", "irreducible; named, no body") }

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **Z-1** | `≈ → ≡ → ≈` | ... ⚠️ **CONTINGENT — it exists only because of the `N-1` definitional conflict.** ... | **Z-4** | `congruence → ≡ → δ → congruence` | ... ✅ **NECESSARY** — **this is Step 288's Z-1 hypothesis, CONFIRMED**
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and evidences the four reconstructed cycles individually: Z-1 (approx<->equiv, CONTINGENT, exists only because 261.5/261.21 define approx and equiv_K by one formula while 261.1/246 list them distinct -- the N-1 conflict; disappears once N-1 resolves); Z-2 (congruence<->equiv, NECESSARY, both directions explicit in 258.9 alone: congruence stated in terms of equiv, and equiv's adequacy judged by congruence); Z-3 (approx->equiv->bindings->approx, NECESSARY given 261.19's per-operation bindings feeding back to approx); Z-4 (congruence->equiv->delta->congruence, NECESSARY, matching and confirming Step 288's own Z-1 hypothesis about delta's postconditions needing equiv while congruence is a property of delta).

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\textbf{ALL FOUR cycles contain } \equiv. \textbf{ NOT ONE contains } \mathcal O \textbf{ or } \mathcal T.}$$ ... **Step 288 reported *"three dependency cycles, all through one node; the bootstrap boundary is `𝒪`/`𝒯`."* Both halves fail**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central refutation directly: Step 288 reported three dependency cycles all through one node, with the bootstrap boundary being O/T ratification; both halves are shown false -- the reconstructed graph has FOUR cycles, not three, and O/T are members of NONE of them. O and T are upstream sources that gate downstream derivation but do not participate in the feedback (cyclic) structure themselves.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ⚠️ **How the error happened, since it matters methodologically:** Step 288 traced each cycle to a node it *depended on* and concluded that node was *in* the cycle. **Being a prerequisite of a cycle is not being a member of it.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagnoses the methodological root cause of Step 288's O/T bootstrap-boundary error: it traced each cycle back to a node the cycle's members depended on (O, T) and concluded that upstream node was itself part of the cycle -- but being a prerequisite of a cyclic structure is not the same as being a member of the cycle. Explicitly identified as the same class of error as the mandate's level-discipline warning (section 16, dependency != blocker), applied one level up (upstream source != cycle member).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ## §4 Robustness — does each cycle survive deletion? ... $$\boxed{\textbf{Three of four cycles survive every deletion.}}$$ ⚠️ **Z-1 is different in kind:** it is a **documentary defect** masquerading as a dependency. It should be repaired (`N-1`), not cut.
b_rows_sample.statement: Robustness-tests each of the four cycles against deletion of philosophical material, verification-lane material, and historical/non-normative definitions: Z-2, Z-3, and Z-4 survive all three deletions (grounded in a single normative-intent corpus section, 258.9 or 261.19), confirming the dependency structure is not an artifact of the philosophical programme or the verification lane; Z-1 alone DIES under deletion of historical material, because it is literally made of the historical duplication between 258.8 and 261.1 -- diagnosed as a documentary defect masquerading as a dependency, which should be repaired via decision N-1, not treated as a structural cycle to be cut.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **27 nodes · 42 edges.** Every edge is **definitional or operational**. Co-mention is **not** an edge (mandate §3): edges were admitted only where a cited passage states that B *requires something from* A.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the admission criterion used to build the 27-node/42-edge graph: an edge A->B is admitted only where a cited corpus passage explicitly states B requires something from A; mere textual co-mention of two concepts is explicitly excluded as insufficient grounds for an edge, per the governing mandate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **`K → ≡_𝒯`** | `258.12` states an **IDENTIFICATION** (`K ≝ ℋ/≡_𝒯`), not a two-way dependency. **An equation rendered as two opposed edges is a modelling artifact**
b_rows_sample.statement: Documents the one edge removed by audit and explains why: 258.12's K := H/equiv_T is a definitional IDENTIFICATION, not a two-way causal dependency, so rendering it as two opposed graph edges (K->equiv_T and equiv_T->K) is a modelling artifact that creates a spurious cycle -- K does not determine equiv_T, T does (retaining the T->equiv_T edge, per Step 260's indexing claim). Both the pre-fix (43-edge, 5-cycle) and post-fix (42-edge, 4-cycle) graphs are deliberately retained in the transcripts so the audit itself is auditable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **hard blocker** | `𝒪` · `𝒯` · `𝒪_K` · `≡` · `δ` · `Qualify` | ... **implementation prerequisite** | `state_rep` · `=` · `projection` | ... **Not every dependency is inflated into a blocker: 8 of 27 nodes are derivable prerequisites.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies all 27 graph nodes into six dependency-vs-blocker categories per the mandate's section 16 requirement: hard blockers (O, T, O_K, equiv, delta, Qualify); soft dependencies (policy->delta, evidence->canonicalization); derivable prerequisites (approx, congruence, minimality, bindings, canonicalization, merge, invariants, sufficiency -- 8 nodes); governance prerequisites (Pi, id_context, assertion, temporal); implementation prerequisites (state_rep, struct_eq, projection); and one documentation dependency (the cong/equiv glyph overloading). b_rows_sample.anchor: $$\boxed{\textbf{F — NOT ESTABLISHED. And, as stated, REFUTED.}}$$ ... ⚠️ **What survives of the Step 288 claim:** `𝒪`/`𝒯` **is** a hard blocker ... **That part stands.** What fails is the inference from *"it is an unresolved prerequisite of the cycles"* to *"it is the cycle-breaking node."*
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies Step 288's bootstrap claim ('the bootstrap boundary is O/T ratification, decidable by authority rather than derivation') against the mandate's six-point A-F scale as F: not established, and as literally stated, refuted -- executed evidence shows cutting {O,T} leaves all four cycles intact, while cutting {equiv} alone is the unique minimal cut, and structurally O/T are not members of any cycle (upstream sources only). What survives of the original claim: O/T genuinely is a hard blocker with no incoming derivation edge found, so that part stands; what fails is the further inference from 'unresolved prerequisite of the cycles' to 'the cycle-breaking node.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: | derive `𝒪` from `K` | 🔴 circular ... | derive from the ratified 8 primitives | 🔴 ... the 8 have **never been shown minimal against an operation space** | enumerate the forced lower bound | 🟡 `256.2`/`259.7` give **14 forced, upper bound 18** ... | **declare membership** | ✅ the only route with no unmet precondition
b_rows_sample.statement: Systematically tests five candidate derivation routes into the operation set O / transformation set T from already-ratified material, finding all fail except direct declaration: deriving O from K is circular (K is downstream of minimality<-congruence<-T); deriving from the invariant universe is blocked since invariants are downstream of equiv (Step 287); deriving from a minimality proof fails since Step 259 states no valid minimality proof exists before transformation-congruence analysis; deriving from the ratified 8 primitives fails since those primitives have never been shown minimal against any operation space; enumerating the forced lower bound (256.2/259.7 give 14 forced operations, upper bound 18) yields only a candidate set, never a membership rule. Only direct governance declaration of membership has no unmet precondition. Concludes: no derivation route to O/T was found in ratified material -- explicitly framed as an absence of evidence for an incoming edge, not a proof that none exists, following the corpus's own absence-of-evidence-stays-Unknown discipline (225.11/224.11); a later step finding a derivation route would SUPERSEDE, not contradict, this finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `261.23`: *"final kernel selection must stop while **equality** remains ambiguous."* **The corpus located the block at equality. Step 288's `𝒪`/`𝒯` gloss moved it, and the computed graph moves it back.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes that the computed minimal cut ({equiv}) independently confirms Step 261.23's own original wording ('final kernel selection must stop while equality remains ambiguous') via a graph-theoretic method Step 261 never used -- the corpus located the block at equality all along; Step 288's O/T gloss had silently moved it, and the fresh computation moves it back to where 261 originally placed it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **ACYCLICITY boundary** | **`{≡}`** | breaks all four feedback loops | resolving it is **NORMATIVE** ... | **DERIVATION boundary** | **`{𝒪, 𝒯}`** | unblocks the 8 derivable prerequisites ... $$\boxed{\text{Cutting the cycles} \neq \text{unblocking the derivation.}}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two genuinely different, both-needed boundaries that Step 288's single 'bootstrap boundary' phrase had conflated: the ACYCLICITY boundary {equiv}, which breaks all four feedback loops (resolving it is normative, tied to N-1 and Decision 3), and the DERIVATION boundary {O,T}, which unblocks the eight derivable prerequisites (approx, congruence, minimality, bindings, canonicalization, merge, invariants, sufficiency) but is itself also normative since no derivation route was found. b_rows_sample.anchor: `≡` can be resolved **two ways**, and they are not equivalent: **by declaration** ... **by derivation** — select `≡` by requiring congruence (`258.9`); **needs `𝒯` and `δ` first** ... **So `{≡}` is a cut only under the *declaration* route. Under the derivation route the cycle reasserts itself**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the precise sense in which the equality problem is genuinely underdetermined by the formal material: equiv can be resolved either by declaration (a governance act fixing equiv, which breaks the cycles immediately and does not need O) or by derivation (selecting equiv by requiring congruence per 258.9, which needs T and delta first) -- and these two routes are not equivalent, since {equiv} is a valid cut only under the declaration route; under the derivation route the cycle reasserts itself through T->congruence->equiv. No recommendation between the two routes is made, this being N-1/N-2 territory.

a_rows_sample.statement: Task 2 mandates reconstructing K from first principles across every serious candidate (10-point per-candidate checklist: source, semantics, type, constructors, equality, membership, admissible/invalid states, instantiability, component-definedness), compared on 15 mathematical criteria, explicitly forbidding selecting the newest or most-component-rich candidate by default, using a 7-value closed verdict vocabulary, output to K-CANDIDATE-COMPARISON.md.

a_rows_sample.statement: Task 6 mandates constructing and actually instantiating the smallest possible concrete toy knowledge state (one proposition, evidence item, context, epistemic status, temporal validity interval, uncertainty representation, provenance relation) and computing 10 operations on it (membership, equality, contradiction, supersession, addition, removal, transformation, validation, provenance lookup, state transition), stopping and recording the exact missing definition wherever an operation cannot be computed -- pseudo-code does not count as execution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determine whether the theory requires a typed family such as: KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History rather than one universal kernel. ... a_rows_sample.statement: Task 8 mandates formally testing whether knowledge must be separated from governance into a typed family of 6 distinct object kinds (KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History) rather than forced into one universal kernel -- a DDD question as much as a mathematical one, asking of every object whether it is a state, relation, operation, assessment, constraint, actor-dependent authorization, or historical property, forbidding forcing all nouns into entities or all concepts into state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: origin -> refinement -> contradiction -> resolution -> current definition. ... RETAINED, REFINED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, HISTORICAL ONLY, VERIFIER PROPOSAL. ... the proper way to preserve the evolutionary nature of the corpus without assuming newer = correct.
